evidence.notes: R-related to EI-10717 (see its note) — the ATTRIBUTION half: apps/operator-vite owns a typecheck ratchet that counts FOREIGN errors from packages it imports but does not own, so an error introduced in operator-core reds a stranger's gate and lands on whoever next touches operator-vite. PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED, deliberately NOT discarded: the specific mechanism this item asked for — operator-core having a typecheck of its own — now EXISTS as `npm run lint:tsc` (scripts/lint-tsc.mjs:167, `tsc -p packages/operator-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so operator-core errors are catchable at their own boundary. What I did NOT verify is whether lint:tsc is ENFORCED anywhere automatic (a green-checkpoint gate step, a CI job) as opposed to being a lever agents are told to run by hand. That distinction decides the whole item: an unenforced typecheck does not stop a foreign error from reaching operator-vite's ratchet, so the attribution defect would survive its own fix. Merit left UNTRIAGED for exactly that reason rather than guessed in either direction.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## The symptom
The rig (Lm1ABoMR), running a bundle that CONTAINS fix C (composedAt 2026-07-27T11:44:22Z), receives the canonical key in a refusal every single tick and never adopts it:

```
[2026-07-27T11:51:22.768Z] [git-sync] papercusp: ref-announce receive fetch FAILED for
IXfGu216EI/z (event 441080); holding cursor at 440845 to re-dial next tick:
no git process ran: duplex error: pot-git serve refused: superseded-repo-key:gh-1223568103
```

Five of these in a single tick. The correct canonical key `gh-1223568103` is sitting in the error text. Nothing adopts it. The rig's `papercusp.git` still holds ZERO namespaces.

## The root cause — reachability, not logic
`adoptRefusedRepoKey` is correct and well-guarded. It has exactly ONE production call site:

- `git-sync-action.ts:2034` — inside the BOOTSTRAP leg's dial path.

But the refusal that carries the repair arrives on a DIFFERENT leg: the ref-announce RECEIVE leg (`git-sync-action.ts:~2345`, the `cursorDecision.fetchFailed` loop). That loop has `f.stderr` containing the verbatim refusal text — and does nothing with it but `console.warn`.

So the one channel on which the repair reliably and repeatedly arrives is the one channel that cannot act on it.

## Why this is the mirror image of fix D
Fix D's own comment (git-sync-action.ts:1839) says the probe must sit ABOVE the warm gate because "a probe placed after the gate would never fire on precisely the machine that needs it: the stuck one." Fix C has the same defect in a different dimension: its receiver is on the cold-join path, so it never runs on the machine whose ref-announce leg is the thing actually dialing.

## The fix
Call `adoptRefusedRepoKey` from the ref-announce receive leg's fetchFailed handler, using `f.stderr` — the same fail-soft, next-tick-effective contract the bootstrap call site already uses. Adoption is idempotent (`already-canonical` is a clean no-op on every later refused dial), so calling it from both legs is safe by construction.

## Broader lesson (worth keeping)
A REFUSAL THAT CARRIES ITS OWN REPAIR ONLY HEALS IF EVERY LEG THAT CAN RECEIVE IT KNOWS HOW TO READ IT. Wiring the receiver into one leg makes the feature look done and tested while leaving it inert on the live path.

evidence.notes: PREMISE VERIFIED AND THE DEFECT IS LARGER THAN FILED. The item reports that sibling work-items can share one payload.plan_item stamp, so completing a SUB-LANE child flips its PARENT's plan item to done via finishPlanStamp(), and states 126 plan items affected with 51 still live. Measured 2026-08-22 over harness_shared.work_items in papercusp-workspace: 4,602 stamped rows across 4,337 distinct (plan_slug,item_id) stamps, of which 200 stamps are SHARED by more than one row, spanning 465 rows, and 83 of those shared stamps still have at least one live (non-done/dropped/deprecated) sibling. So the true figures are 200 affected stamps (filed: 126) and 83 with a live sibling (filed: 51) — the filer UNDER-CLAIMED by ~1.6x on both. That is the THIRD independent confirmation of D-026 s4's direction-of-error rule, on a third unrelated finding, and it is now safe to treat "a filed number is a floor to re-measure" as established rather than suggestive. R-related to EI-20577421906951067, not a duplicate: this one is the OVER-FIRE (things get closed that should not be), that one is the IRREVERSIBILITY (a wrong closure cannot be undone). They are two halves of one trap and neither is safe to fix alone — fixing only the over-fire leaves existing bad closures stuck; fixing only the reopen path leaves the source of them running. Both are complaints against the very reconciler whose existence supersedes EI-2443/EI-2725 in this same batch.

report.message: durable admission record could not be persisted: canceling statement due to lock timeout | sqlstate=55P03 — task exits 1 and is counted as a test failure; retry re-hits the same error

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED in the canonical run 7 log (/tmp/p005-run7-runlog.stripped, run=241941-199610b3).

The task `@papercusp/operator-core :: lint:prompt-projections` emitted:

  AFFECTED_TASK_OUTPUT_BEGIN task="@papercusp/operator-core :: lint:prompt-projections" label=initial lane=serial workers=15 memoryMb=15360 exitStatus=1 signal=none error="durable admission record could not be persisted: canceling statement due to lock timeout | sqlstate=55P03"

and the SAME error on its `label=retry` attempt.

WHY THIS IS A BUG, not just an unlucky run:

1. FALSE RED. The guard itself is green. Re-run at HEAD: `node scripts/check-prompt-projections.mjs` exits 0 — canonical libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/su.md (sha256 0b998acc8bf0d3c3d128edc021ad4c5e31860df6905ecd61c003ebf8c8df72bb, 74226 bytes) matches both generated projections, mismatches=[]. The exit 1 was produced by the admission layer, not the check.

2. INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GENUINE FAILURE. The task surfaces only as exitStatus=1. It landed in `unattributed` (reason=no-file-rows) purely because it emits no per-file rows — i.e. it was excluded from the file-level accounting by accident of shape, not because anything recognized it as infrastructure. A guard that DID emit file rows would have been reported as a plain red with no hint that the cause was a lock timeout.

3. THE RETRY DOES NOT RECOVER IT. Both attempts failed on the identical sqlstate=55P03. A retry that re-enters the same contended write path cannot clear a lock-timeout class, so the retry budget is spent without changing the outcome.

CONSEQUENCE. This inflates a canonical run's failure count with non-verdicts. The repo already has the correct concept — capability:bash_output distinguishes failure_class=infrastructure-resource-limit with test_verdict=undetermined, and the plan's own D-006/D-019 say an undetermined run is not a verdict — but affected-tests does not apply it here. On a full-suite run that must exit 0 to satisfy P-004, an infrastructure lock timeout is currently able to block the gate indefinitely, and every agent triaging it will go read a guard that is perfectly green.

CORRECT STATE. An admission/ledger persistence failure should mark the task `undetermined` with an explicit infrastructure failure_class — never fold it into the failed-task count as if the task's own command had failed — and the retry path should either back off against lock contention or report that it re-hit the same infrastructure class rather than consuming an attempt silently.

externalBlockers.evidence:
MEASURED 2026-09-02T16:2xZ.

CONDITION REPRODUCES: harness_shared.admission_runs (harness_slug='papercusp', 26h) GROUP BY run_kind/detail.mode/detail.status —
  promoter-tick / fail-open / complete  52  last 16:18   <- healthy
  promoter-tick / promoter  / FAILED    24  last 16:09   <- the defect
  promoter-tick / promoter  / complete  28  last 04:00   <- 745m ago, threshold 90m
  delta-sweep   / -         / FAILED    15  last 16:15
So "no successful promoter tick for ~745m" holds right now; the item is NOT stale despite freshness likelyStale=true.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not inferred):
1. Every failed promoter run AND every failed delta-sweep run carries detail.error verbatim "The usage limit has been reached". That string appears NOWHERE in the repo (grep -rn over packages/apps/libs = 0 hits), so it is an upstream refusal, not our code.
2. model_id IS NULL on all 24 promoter failures — the refusal lands before a model is selected, i.e. at account/dispatch level.
3. The dispatch path is codex: work-items-admission-promoter.ts:1943 resolves `opts.model?.trim() || LEARNING_MODEL_SPEC`, and LEARNING_MODEL_SPEC = 'gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh' (learning/model-policy.ts:21-23).
4. NO per-routine override exists: payload_template->>'model' IS NULL for all 12 %admission% routines, so the constant is what actually runs.
5. accounts:probe-capacity { provider:'codex' } at 16:2xZ returned probed:7, unwalled:[], serving:[], confirmedWalled:[chatgpt-sub-cli, aviynw2_codex, aviynw_3, aviynw4_codex, aviynw5_codex, aviynw3_codex, aviynw6_codex] — all 7 status 429, utilization7d 1.0. This is the live upstream reading, not the accounts:status projection.

BLAST RADIUS: exactly the LLM-backed admission routines — promoter + delta-sweep (both failing on the same string). work-item-admission-fail-open is a SEPARATE deterministic runner that makes no model call, still firing (16:18) and admitting rows as admission='unreviewed'. That is why queue distribution is NOT starved, as the item's own text says.

SCOPE LIMIT: this probe measured the DEFAULT (sol/generic) codex bucket, which is the one the promoter uses. It says nothing about the 'gpt-reserve' (luna) bucket.

NOT ACTIONABLE AS AN ENGINEERING FIX: the item's stated ask, "Restore the durable work-item-admission-promoter routine", has no code repair — the routine is active (last_fired_at 16:02, next_fire_at 16:30) and correct. Do not "fix" the promoter.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## What I measured

`routines:list { name:'work-item-admission-promoter', installSlug:'papercusp' }` at 2026-09-02T22:31Z:

```
cron: 0 */30 * * * *   active: true   targetRole: system:work-item-admission-promoter
lastFiredAt: 2026-09-02T22:30:57.254Z
nextFireAt:  2026-09-02T23:00:00.000Z
health: { last_error: "The usage limit has been reached" }
```

The routine is **firing on schedule and failing inside the tick.** Its sibling `work-item-admission-fail-open` is healthy (`health: null`, fired 22:16:53Z, next 22:45).

Admission census, `harness_shared.work_items`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`, last 6h, `lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation'`:

| admission | n | oldest | newest |
|---|---|---|---|
| (null) | 949 | 16:31 | 22:30 |
| unreviewed | 76 | 16:32 | **21:10** |
| auto | 34 | 16:41 | 22:17 |
| pending | 17 | **21:28 (64 min)** | 22:22 |

The oldest `pending` row is **past the 60-minute fail-open guarantee** the claim refusal advertises, and no fail-open promotion has landed since 21:10.

## Verified at the source, not inferred from bucket names

`work-items-admission-promoter.ts:2179` — `SET admission = 'unreviewed', admitted_at = now(), admitted_by = ${FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR} ... AND admission = 'pending'`. So `unreviewed` is written by the FAIL-OPEN path specifically. That is what makes the census above readable: a growing `pending` bucket with a frozen `unreviewed` high-water mark is the promoter not screening, with the backstop not yet eligible.

## The actual defect — the silence, not the outage

A `system:*` targetRole means this routine is LLM-backed, so account starvation takes out its whole tick. A coord broadcast at ~22:32Z reads `infra-liveness RECOVERED (accounts-starved)`, which names the mechanism and says it has since cleared — so this instance is a self-recovering flap.

That does not make it a non-issue, for one reason: **the degraded mode is indistinguishable from the healthy one at every surface an agent or operator actually looks at.**

- Items still get admitted, so nothing appears broken.
- They are admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` — i.e. **never duplicate-screened at all** — which is precisely the safety property admission exists to provide.
- The only trace is `health.last_error` on the routine row. Nothing raises it, and the claim-refusal text an agent sees says only "this floor CLEARS ON ITS OWN", which reads as normal operation.
- Latency silently doubles: every item rides the 60-minute backstop instead of the 30-minute screened path.

So during any account-starvation window, duplicate screening across the workspace is quietly OFF while continuing to look on. That is the same defect class this tree treats as first-order everywhere else — a bounded/failed instrument whose output is indistinguishable from a real result.

Worth noting as a plausible instance rather than a proven one: I minted **four duplicate consults** on one plan earlier today. I have not established a causal link and am not claiming one; it is the kind of outcome this failure mode would produce.

## Suggested fix, in preference order

1. **Make the degradation loud.** When the promoter's tick fails, emit/alert rather than only stamping `health.last_error`. A silently fail-open screening gate is the whole bug.
2. **Distinguish the two admissions the census cannot.** `unreviewed` currently conflates "screened and found clean" with "never screened, admitted by timeout". `admitted_by = FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` already carries the truth — surface it wherever admission state is read, so a fail-open backlog is visible as one.
3. **Survive partial starvation.** A per-item try/catch with backoff would let a tick screen what it can instead of losing the whole batch to the first usage-limit rejection.

## Reproduction

Starve the account the `system:work-item-admission-promoter` role routes through, then file an unassigned work-item and watch: the promoter tick errors, the item sits `pending` for the full 60 minutes, and is then admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` having never been screened.

## Note on this filing

Filed unassigned, so this item will itself sit in the `pending` queue it describes — a usable end-to-end check of the behaviour above.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Observation (measured, not inferred)
- The shared QEMU VM serving the windows smoke rig on 127.0.0.1:2223 has been UP 12 days 18 hours, continuously consuming ~8 vCPUs.
- Its sshd NEVER answers: the connection reaches banner exchange and times out. The PORT IS LISTENING, so any probe that checks reachability rather than a completed handshake reads it as healthy.
- The mac rig on :2222 answers but REJECTS the provisioned `papercup-vm-mac` key.
- Host context: `/` is at 99% (35 GB free of 1.9 TB) and this box runs the whole agent fleet. 8 cores burned continuously for 12+ days is a large invisible tax on every other lane.

## Two distinct defects, deliberately not conflated
1. **The VM is wedged and nobody noticed for 12+ days.** A LISTENING port with a never-completing handshake is the worst available failure shape: invisible to a port probe, surfacing only when someone needs it — which is always mid-release.
2. **There is no detector.** Nothing alarms on a QEMU guest pegging N cores for days, and nothing alarms on a smoke rig that has served no successful run in N days. The second is the one that matters — this is a DETECTOR FAILURE, not merely a wedged process.

## Consequence for releases
The platform-smoke gate is the ONLY gate that exercises an INSTALLED artifact. Provenance and signatures prove the bytes are the bytes we built and signed; they prove nothing about whether the installer RUNS. With the rig wedged, every release since it died has had to override that gate — and an override that is unavoidable every single time stops being a decision and becomes a formality.

## Correction to a claim I was carrying (on the record as FALSE)
I nearly justified the override with a carried note saying the build VM is retired. That was FALSE. WI-5651 retired those VMs as BUILD legs; the SMOKE rig is a separate thing, both ports are live, and a genuine 0.0.19 windows smoke receipt exists on disk from 2026-09-09. The correct justification is that the rig is WEDGED — an evidenced exception. Same override either way, but only one of the two is honest in a ship record.

## Evidence
- `ss -ltnp | grep 222` → :2222 and :2223 both LISTENING.
- `timeout 8 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -p 2223 -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win user@127.0.0.1 true` → timeout at banner exchange; no auth attempt reached.
- The 0.0.21-alpha ship record carries this verbatim as the smoke-gate override reason (/tmp/upload-real.log).

## Durable fix (not just a restart)

_claimSubjectBaseline.title: Wedged QEMU smoke-rig VM has pegged 8 vCPUs for 12+ days and silently decayed the platform-smoke ship gate into a formality
_claimSubjectBaseline.summary:
## Observation (measured, not inferred)
- The shared QEMU VM serving the windows smoke rig on 127.0.0.1:2223 has been UP 12 days 18 hours, continuously consuming ~8 vCPUs.
- Its sshd NEVER answers: the connection reaches banner exchange and times out. The PORT IS LISTENING, so any probe that checks reachability rather than a completed handshake reads it as healthy.
- The mac rig on :2222 answers but REJECTS the provisioned `papercup-vm-mac` key.
- Host context: `/` is at 99% (35 GB free of 1.9 TB) and this box runs the whole agent fleet. 8 cores burned continuously for 12+ days is a large invisible tax on every other lane.

## Two distinct defects, deliberately not conflated
1. **The VM is wedged and nobody noticed for 12+ days.** A LISTENING port with a never-completing handshake is the worst available failure shape: invisible to a port probe, surfacing only when someone needs it — which is always mid-release.
2. **There is no detector.** Nothing alarms on a QEMU guest pegging N cores for days, and nothing alarms on a smoke rig that has served no successful run in N days. The second is the one that matters — this is a DETECTOR FAILURE, not merely a wedged process.

## Consequence for releases
The platform-smoke gate is the ONLY gate that exercises an INSTALLED artifact. Provenance and signatures prove the bytes are the bytes we built and signed; they prove nothing about whether the installer RUNS. With the rig wedged, every release since it died has had to override that gate — and an override that is unavoidable every single time stops being a decision and becomes a formality.

## Correction to a claim I was carrying (on the record as FALSE)
I nearly justified the override with a carried note saying the build VM is retired. That was FALSE. WI-5651 retired those VMs as BUILD legs; the SMOKE rig is a separate thing, both ports are live, and a genuine 0.0.19 windows smoke receipt exists on disk from 2026-09-09. The correct justification is that the rig is WEDGED — an evidenced exception. Same override either way, but only one of the two is honest in a ship record.

## Evidence
- `ss -ltnp | grep 222` → :2222 and :2223 both LISTENING.
- `timeout 8 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -p 2223 -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win user@127.0.0.1 true` → timeout at banner exchange; no auth attempt reached.
- The 0.0.21-alpha ship record carries this verbatim as the smoke-gate override reason (/tmp/upload-real.log).

## Durable fix (not just a restart)
Restart/rebuild the guest (recovers 8 cores) and re-provision the mac rig key — then add the MISSING DETECTOR: alarm when a smoke rig has served no successful run in N days, so the gate cannot silently decay again. A restart alone leaves the trap armed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Suspected operator event-loop defect: an earlier dev:service_health sample recorded :3070 accept backlog 45/511 and a 3011ms probe timeout while the systemd unit remained active; the same sample recorded majorFaultDelta=0, memory PSI full=0 and swap=0, followed by HTTP 200 and nRestarts=0. New targeted papercusp-dev-api.service logs show the sentinel reported STALLED at 02:58:57.896Z after 10,018ms (main thread spinning, state R, 0.99 cores, CPU PSI some60=5.4), then SIGKILLed request-worker PID 2970199 at 02:59:11.910Z after 24,031ms (mode kill, 20,000ms threshold, 0.98 cores, PSI=5.77). At 02:59:22 a PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 secondary host booted; the live systemd operator unit nRestarts=0 supports worker respawn without a unit restart, so the title remains accurate. Same-window bounded-timeout lines for turn-start executable frontier and agent-obligations show slow work but do not identify a caller; system journal had no OOM/hung-task/lockup matches. This establishes a nearby request-worker CPU-spin class, not exact linkage to the earlier 02:57 sample or the JS frame. The prior carry-note statement that 02:50–03:05Z had zero service-journal entries was wrong. The worker is gone, so its JS stack cannot be recovered. No code change is justified from this trace alone: on the next recurrence, act on the first STALLED line (~10s stale), send SIGUSR1 to the reported Node PID, capture /json/list and a 3–5s V8 sampling profile before the 20s kill threshold, plus per-thread /proc state/wchan/cgroup and unit+system journals. See agent-insights/profiling-a-wedged-node-host-runbook.

WI-10004909 records git-sync's declaration inventory and superproject commits blocked until read-tree rebuilt the index. The truncating writer remains unidentified; coincident git-sync/bg-host activity does not establish responsibility.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-05 ~20:20Z while running the grading-integrity audit of EI-25171788938691287 (audit EI-25172375455718591, judge session su-b50e85cc).

The graded card's prefer-structured-check evidence pins its proof to a commit: 'Reproduce via git show 9e2fba799e7d4c0bd426415e9834c2cf3bd4f8ab:<path>'. It also claims the current bytes of all 10 bound test paths equal that commit's blobs. The grading-integrity rubric's re-runnable-evidence drill says to 'execute each evidence probe exactly as written', and the kickoff brief says 'Preserve the stored evidence scope; do not substitute a newer working tree'.

The judge-scoped MCP principal ('system:judge') is refused every read-only route to commit-pinned content:
- capability:git → missing_capability (show / rev-parse / hash-object all unavailable)
- dev:pg_query → missing_capability intel:read
- dev:pipeline_position → role_not_allowed (judge is not on the allowlist)

So the auditor can only read the WORKING TREE with capability:read, which is exactly the substitution the brief forbids. In this audit, three consult-routing-health.test.ts titles cited at :168/:205/:214 sit at :173/:207/:216 in the working tree. Whether that is drift after the commit or a citation error could not be determined: the commit could not be read.

Proposed fix (smallest extension, reuse-first): grant the judge role a read-only git subset (show <sha>:<path>, rev-parse <sha>:<path>, hash-object <path>, log -1 -- <path>) on capability:git. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-05 ~21:30Z while running the grading-integrity audit of EI-25176403929067237 (judge session, system:judge principal, build 8bb88cd105).

Symptom: the card's only evidenceRefs were thread-post:1158166 (6679 chars) and thread-post:1158172 (7013 chars). Reading them was much harder than it should be:
1. conversations:get {id:'thread-post:1158166'} via tools:invoke returned post.body cut to ~1100 chars plus a scratch-page cursor ("[TRUNCATED +5879 chars]").
2. capability:read {file_path:<that scratch .md>, raw:true} refused with scratch_line_window_too_large, because the spill is one JSON line. The documented alternative is byte pages of base64, which a model cannot read directly.
3. code:run returning body.slice() chunks still had each string capped at ~400 chars ("[truncated 1104 chars]"). One run returning 10x380 chars spilled again to a papercusp.output-envelope/v1 (shared result-door budget).
4. What worked: 8 sequential code:run calls, each returning 5x380-char windows. Two posts took 8 model turns.

Why it matters: every grading-integrity auditor of a meta-acceptance-rubric attestation has to read these consult critique posts, which are routinely ~7k chars, so this cost repeats on every audit.

Proposed fix (either one):
(a) conversations:get accepts {bodyOffset, bodyLimit} (or bodyWindow) for thread-post refs, so a reader can page the body as plaintext; or
(b) capability:read raw:true on a single-line scratch spill splits that line into plaintext char windows (offset/limit by chars) instead of refusing.
Option (b) fixes every tool's spills, not just conversations:get.

Unconfirmed: whether a superuser (non-judge) session gets a larger per-field cap.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Original retrieval and security continuations are omitted from coordination while their matching PSU PTY hosts remain live, so coord:send refuses unknown_recipient and a correct fork:false resume refuses duplicate live ownership.

Measured evidence (2026-11-06; complete receipts at EI-25180316715417887#1217033 and EI-28081291096944491#1217034): exact workspace-scoped ADV reads with a passing same-table control returned rows55265/55262, matching original owner/native UUIDs, ended_atNULL, started2026-11-05, outside the current10-minute recorded bootstrap window, and no coord_presence rows. Matching host metadata binds those same owner/ADV/native identities with sockets present. Targeted reconciled task-ledger rows remain running. Supported current3170 explicit-false resumes refused LIVE before spawning anyprocess. This proves the roster/host disagreement; why the hosted CLIs did not re-register presence is still unknown.

Cause of the observed addressability failure: recipient-resolve.ts/readKnownOwnerIds consults presence and listRecordedLiveSessions, whose default started_at cutoff is RECORDED_ADV_SESSION_FRESH_SEC=600. resolveResumeTarget instead checks verified findLiveHostAsync. Thus an older genuine local host can be correctly protected against duplicate resume but absent from the message-recipient roster. Do not fix this by widening a timeout/age limit, accepting arbitrary unknown IDs, forging presence, killing the old host or creating a replacement.

Reuse-first repair proposal: extend the existing targeted recipient path with getLatestActiveAdvSessionByOwner(exactOwner,workspace), already age-independent and newest-row scoped, plus existing verified findLiveHostAsync. Require exact owner, workspace and immutable ADV binding agreement; preserve ended/superseded/retired rejection, prefix ambiguity, caller/assignee rules and cached broad-roster behavior. No global PTY-directory scan or parallel identity authority. Add maintained recipient-resolve.test.ts regression coverage for aged-out genuine local sessions and wrong workspace/owner/ADV, stale host, superseded record and ordinary roster/prefix cases. Current source/tests have NOT been edited or run.

Acceptance: normal coord addressing and wake delivery must reach the original continuation through its correct identity, with fresh pickup proof, while duplicate-owner resume and cross-workspace guards continue to refuse. This does not clear retrieval D011/P008, security selection/corpus/legal, native qualification, review or shipment holds. The old unexpected-fork serving-generation defect stays separately owned as EI-28081291096944491.

Canonical review adoption assigned this revision-requested item to su-78560746-d1a0-423b-a26e-c1e9c6486454. Implementation claim was refused at agent-review/not-ready; no code changes were made around that floor. This revision supplies the measured condition and bounded reuse plan for independent review.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-08 ~02:50–03:20Z from a judge-scoped session (grading-integrity audit of EI-25377456345340418, run 1791427485-judge), all via mcp__papercusp__tools_invoke on serving build d5faa7963f.

Symptoms (Claude Code MCP idle timeout = 300s with no progress):
- code:run looping scorecards:get over 9 criteria → no response/progress for 300s, aborted (task k9u5j2meg).
- scorecards:get {issueId:'EI-25377456345340418', criterionKey:'correct-layer', evidenceOffset:2274} → no response for 300s, aborted (k30bpfz06); the IDENTICAL call re-issued minutes later returned normally, so it is not payload size.
- scorecards:list {rubricRef:'spec-test-adequacy', subjectRef:'…'} → no response for 300s, aborted (ke115097e).
- plans:get-spec-evidence {slug, specIds:['RECOVERY-R-4-MISSING'], detail:'full'} → >120s; testing:runs {filePath, sinceHours:24} → >120s; scorecards:list {rubricRef, limit:100} → >120s.
- improvements:capture (this filing) first attempt shed: mcp_proxy_improvements_capture_queue_dwell, waited 20001ms in the dedicated FIFO (traceId 933196f2-26be-40b8-a6c8-e979a33c3a94).
Other calls in the same session (rubrics:get, several scorecards:get pages, plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy) returned in seconds, so the latency is intermittent rather than tied to one tool.

Cause UNKNOWN / unconfirmed. Untested hypotheses: serving-host event-loop saturation, PG pool contention, or proxy FIFO backlog. Suggested probe: harness_shared.tool_invocations for this owner over 02:45–03:20Z; compare durations by tool_name and serving_host, and check proxy queue depth at the capture traceId. A 300s silent stall with no progress notification is itself a defect: long calls should stream progress or fail fast.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Unrelated handlers lose output when the shared result-door projection requires overflow persistence but cannot write the scratch spill. EI-25408351848678899 reports an unavailable checkpoint cursor with spill-write-failed; EI-25409580348208359 and EI-25409749057195100 report explicit 30000ms ETIMEDOUT failures on document results; EI-25409763444620761 reports the same failure on directed mail. EI-25410024981236879 and EI-25410269323486697 instead receive empty output_spill_failed envelopes. The same post-handler failure affects mutations: EI-25410122061838770 retains a recorded receipt but loses canonical output, while EI-25410344016199089 confirms a committed emit whose receipt was entirely swallowed behind retryable:true. Repairing the shared persistence/fallback path addresses these manifestations together. Filesystem contention, disk pressure and writer serialization remain unverified; successfully written spills that cannot be read because of single-line truncation are a separate cause.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Different handlers reach the same post-handler result-door scratch writer, then report spill-write-failed/output_spill_failed, commonly ETIMEDOUT after 30000ms. Coordination threads (EI-25424920546318879), document reads (EI-25425159282204609), and transcript tails (EI-25425669800696149) lose overflow without a recoverable cursor. Capture and send mutations retain committed receipts but lose remaining output (EI-25423907483948308, EI-25424167976820667). EI-25423748222711260 shows the delayed variant: a roughly 6KB spill is still pending at the deadline, returns ENOENT immediately, and becomes readable later. EI-25426355936196935 links one failing invocation to scratch quota-wait with pendingWrites=121 and recoveryActive=true; this does not prove the storage cause of every occurrence. Repair the shared persistence, readiness, and recovery path while preserving mutation outcomes separately from projection failures.

EI-25428617195110357 corroborates the shared persistence/recovery boundary. Repair spill settlement and lossless overflow recovery without attributing these failures to /tmp exhaustion, quota, contention or event-loop load absent measurement.

Bounded output depends on a scratch write; failure or a 30000ms deadline leaves omitted bytes unavailable or still pending without a usable lossless fallback. EI-25434486004764046's pending path returns ENOENT; EI-25437870404169638 confirms a write committed before its response spill failed. EI-25436285203845520 corroborates this boundary. WI-10007577 measures failed FIFO eviction at the 5 GiB workspace quota, stale usage caching, and recovery after reclaim/cache refresh; this diagnoses its cohort, not every earlier timeout. Repair spill settlement and preserve a lossless alternate recovery path.

report.message: request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable during the before-batch run authority refresh.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
This item concerns intermittent failure of admin transaction startup during native session verification. The MCP rejection itself is the intentional security boundary: preserve fail-closed verification; do not admit an inherited or unverified native identity.

The original reporter recurrence was captured on 2026-10-09 against b7937697dc. A second encounter occurred during bulk-4903eb58-a140-4b78-b5da-8816ad1309f1 after four allowed acknowledgements and a 100-item recommendation batch. The transcript shows tools:invoke calling inbox:bulk-run-manifest and receiving request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable before any further bulk report/action. The bulk pass subsequently completed through the sanctioned same-owner CLI route; that route's success alone did not establish native-wrapper health.

The exact second failure is tool_invocations:35038620 at 2026-10-10T01:04:07.336Z, coord owner su-7f5e54d1-974b-4603-9aeb-4cf2487f2a1d, serving process linux:b8c61f1d-f67c-43a8-ac9d-2286713e224f:38294679, build a2c76aa503. Its retained mcpAuthFailure is contextVerified=false, with carrier meta:threadId, candidateAdvSessionId=null and valueFingerprint=51d40c49bf5903be8bfae7dc1bbcf951855c4dc1c0ea365275222fc6c41ee1e0. verifierFailure.name=DbCallDeadlineError; phase=transaction_setup; acquisition.label=boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin); pool=org-admin; deadlineMs=7500; elapsedMs=7499; retryable=true. No PostgreSQL error code was retained. verifierFailure.durationMs=201 is a separate measurement from the deadline object's elapsedMs; the record does not establish that this verifier call itself waited 7499ms. The captured pool/ticket counts are seam diagnostics, not evidence of CPU/RAM exhaustion or a saturated pool.

Current-runtime read-only probe: invoke the same manifest read through the native tools:invoke wrapper, using this session's ordinary metadata. It succeeded at 2026-10-10T01:31:59.128Z/129Z, receipts tool_invocations:35052893 (inner) and 35052894 (wrapper). Both have the EXACT SAME serving process, build a2c76aa503, carrier and native-session fingerprint as the failure, and now show binding=bound, candidateAdvSessionId=39357. adv_sessions:39357 belongs to this Codex owner and started at 2026-10-10T00:46:42.032456Z, before the failure. This establishes current binding and identity continuity; it does not retroactively authorize the rejected call. A fresh failure did not reproduce, so reproduced=true is not claimed.

Security/source check: _mcp-host.ts:1880-1896 rejects on verifier exceptions to prevent the inherited-session authorization bug. The existing registered gating suite covers fail-closed rejection, no terminal callback dispatch, redacted diagnostics, and typed acquire/begin/setup deadline fields. Focused test run 20966201 in papercusp/local passed five selected cases; 328 cases were deliberately excluded by the name filter. Command: npm run test:file -- --require-ran packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts -- '--testNamePattern=fails closed with a retryable verifier reason|retains typed .* deadline diagnostics when native verification fails closed'. The unused --require-ran token was treated as a non-test input; actual matched cases and counts are verified in testing:runs. HEAD moved 6fa9ff1f727d to b20fd572c871 during the run, runtime source capture was not configured, and the runner/ledger marked provenance unknown/worktreeDirty=true. These are exploratory guard observations, not build-bound acceptance evidence.

Remaining work: determine why boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin) failed, correlate the relevant verifier request/ticket with transaction/connection diagnostics from that serving process, and establish a durable fix with source-bound regression evidence. The existing current-process completed-query ring does not cover in-flight/acquisition/non-ReadyForQuery failures and cannot substitute for the incident's missing causal trace. The underlying database/startup cause remains unverified. No code change, restart, deadline widening, retry bypass or auth weakening was made. Keep the issue open; no fixed/shipped claim.

terminalCompletionEvidence.verifiedHow: Systemd reports the papercusp-server drop-in loaded and its process environment has PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0. The :3271 operator and MCP handshake both return 200. The dedicated inference gateway is active/healthy with zero probe failures, restartsLast10m=0, flapState=ok, and the aggregate unhealthy-supervision count is 0. The :8788 listener is in the dedicated gateway process tree. Gateway logs show 73 EADDRINUSE entries from 05:18:48.460Z through 07:24:56.564Z, all before the server's 07:27:46Z activation with the override, and none afterward.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: The packaged papercusp-server fallback and the dedicated systemd inference gateway competed to bind :8788, causing repeated EADDRINUSE failures in the dedicated gateway.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: pass: the bind-conflict stream stopped after the server loaded the override, and current ownership and health match the single-gateway hypothesis.

rootCauseVerification.testProcedure: Read papercusp-server.service and papercup-inference-gateway.service journals over the bounded four-hour window with an EADDRINUSE filter; compare log timestamps to the server ActiveEnterTimestamp; inspect systemd Environment/MainPID, the :8788 listener PID and parent chain, and dev:service_health.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: The dedicated gateway journal had 73 EADDRINUSE rows from 2026-10-10T05:18:48.460Z to 07:24:56.564Z, all before the server's 07:27:46Z activation; there were zero such rows afterward. The current server process has PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0. The gateway unit is active/healthy with zero probe failures and flapState=ok, and its process tree owns the :8788 listener.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Timestamp-correlate EADDRINUSE entries from both service units with the server activation that loaded the host-only override; then verify the effective server process environment, :8788 listener process ancestry, and current service health.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The dedicated inference gateway failed independently while no competing server fallback was binding :8788.

predictedObservations.hypothesis: EADDRINUSE entries occur while the server fallback is enabled and stop after PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0 is loaded; the dedicated gateway owns :8788 and becomes healthy.
predictedObservations.alternativeHypothesis: The dedicated gateway continues failing after the server override is active, or the bind-conflict records do not stop at the server activation boundary.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-10-11 ~00:33Z during grading-integrity audit EI-25641212024088928 of spec-test-adequacy card EI-25640783139681422.

Grading-audit kickoff briefs say "Preserve the complete bytes for the cited blob's integrity check". The spec_evidence_bindings.details.measurementPin.files[] rows carry sha256 + headBlob per file. Two examples: binding 35658 pins packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/lsp-daemon-cache.test.ts at sha256 c211755e…, headBlob d5ff3c76…; binding 35687 pins native-ecosystem.test.ts at sha256 8769cc98….

Neither instrument available to a judge can produce a comparable hash:
1. capability:git-evidence { op:'readFileAtCommit' } returns only { ok, op, commitSha, path, bytes, content, _meta }. It has no blob oid and no sha256.
2. code:run has no `crypto` global. Calling `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', …)` threw "crypto is not defined", so the script cannot hash the content itself.
The judge role is also told not to use capability:git or shell. So the blob-to-pin identity can only be taken on trust from server-measured currentness, and the audit has to record that as a gap.

Proposed fix (smallest extension, no new surface): have readFileAtCommit also return `blobOid` (git's own object id) and `sha256` of the returned bytes. Alternatively or additionally, expose a `sha256(string|Uint8Array)` helper in the code:run sandbox. Either one lets an auditor compare directly against measurementPin.files[].sha256/headBlob.

Related: scorecards:get criterion evidence pages are ~2.9KB each (EI-25632408471242790 already tracks that). This audit worked around it by reading the payload via dev:pg_query on harness_shared.work_items.payload->'observation'->'ratings'.

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools` (4 newer commits, tip `9b9e9ae5f8390f9191b31faf0fa06a0845619540`) have commits newer than the running build (`3e02a3af06`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-10-11 00:33Z (su-92de4154). A .papercusp/scratch/*.mts probe calling the real sweepSilentHalts({dryRun:true}) via getOrgPg() returned checked:0, halted:0. That is a clean, plausible zero, but the same probe had checked 118 sessions 4h earlier. The control line showed port 24680 (routine_rows 0) instead of 5432: getHarnessAdminUrlWithSource() prefers the discovery file ~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json, which pointed at a LIVE embedded PG (pid 4112740) over the native :5432 fallback. Re-running with PAPERCUSP_SKIP_PG_DISCOVERY=1 hit 5432 and checked 131. Any agent script on the dev box without HARNESS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL pinned silently measures the wrong database whenever a desktop/verify instance has written the discovery file. Evidence: .papercusp/scratch/p007e-control.out (port 24680, checked 0) vs p007e-untimed-awaits.out (port 5432, checked 130). Suggested durable fix: have scripts report the resolved URL source, or warn on stderr when discovery wins over the native fallback on the dev box. Also add a positive-control line to the probe template.

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts` (5 newer commits, tip `5dd2e8a291163fa8df207d51c5937dd294d136c0`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED 2026-10-11 ~00:59Z (judge su-94c69eb9, grading-integrity audit of EI-25641605517480359): a successful tools:invoke { name:'scorecards:emit' } (completionReceipt recorded, effectRef EI-25642361636963872) came back with _projection.cursor.kind='volatile-scratch-page', reason='spill-write-failed', errorCode='ETIMEDOUT', errorDetail='Error: result-door scratch spill write exceeded 30000ms'. The payload was only 8796 chars. A 30s+ write for a ~9KB spill points to blocked or contended scratch persistence, not payload size. Unconfirmed cause.

Same session, related degraded signals: (a) code:run returns were repeatedly spilled with accounting.summaryBudgetChars=0 and incomplete.reason='aggregate-output-budget-exceeded' / 'under-budget-partial-result' (recoverable:false) for ~6KB summaries, apparently because of concurrent grading-audit judges sharing one result-door budget cohort. (b) Every turn's memory leg timed out, and the query embed exceeded its ~297ms budget.

Impact: the emit is non-idempotent, and the only exact copy of its result lived in an in-process volatile URI that expires in ~15 min and is lost on restart. A caller who cannot read it must reconstruct the outcome from the ledger. Load-correlated (≈400 live peers, many concurrent judges). Expected: a spill of under 10KB persists within the deadline at any load.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-10-11T09:33Z judging WI-6554700010008504 (task 0mv2kuyk2ctvxu6p7qd, unaccounted-residue).

The task_ledger row for this kernel residue is a reconciler-synthesized stub:
  argv = []  (jsonb, empty)   cwd = null   log_path = null   launched_by = "unknown"
  session_id = null, parent_task_id = null, work_item_id = null, plan_slug = null, fleet_slug = null
  title = 200 chars, hard-truncated mid-path: "... systemd-scope-env-runner.mjs --env-fd-path /proc/self/fd/3 -- /home/marsh-office/"

The process is a systemd-scope-env-runner.mjs shim whose entire purpose is to exec an INNER command after the "--". That inner command is the only thing identifying what this residue is. It is truncated away in title, absent from argv, and processes:list exposes no argv/command/cmdline field at all (measured task key set has none).

CONSEQUENCE: the keep/kill judgment turns on whether this is an abandoned rig or a legitimately idle long-lived sidecar — it sits in papercusp-sidecar.slice with 0 CPU for 17.5h, which is normal for an idle sidecar AND consistent with abandonment. With the inner command unrecoverable that question is unanswerable from any available instrument, forcing a perpetual "keep". /proc/<pid>/cmdline is no fallback: capability:bash runs in a separate PID namespace (measured $$=2, 5 visible numeric /proc entries, ns pid:[4026543257]), so host PIDs are invisible there.

SUGGESTED CHANGE: when the reconciler synthesizes a ledger row for an unenrolled pc-*.scope, capture /proc/<pid>/cmdline into argv (and /proc/<pid>/cwd into cwd) at discovery time from the host-visible reconciler context, storing full argv rather than relying on a truncated title. That single field makes an unaccounted-residue verdict decidable instead of indefinitely deferred.

UNCONFIRMED CAUSE — the observation is filed; the mechanism is not proven.

What I saw: during the grading-integrity audit of scorecard EI-25828255998725711 (judge session su-628f4d8c, client papercusp-su via tools:invoke), two read-only code:run calls returned {error:'mcp_proxy_upstream_error', forwardingResult:'outcome_unknown', detail:'read ECONNRESET', attempts:1, windowMs:90000}. traceIds: 27cc7b31-c7d1-481a-9f1d-a9720b184a9f (~2026-10-13T02:10:49Z) and 0c98adaa-8afa-4744-be9d-03bf179b469c (~02:12:10Z). Each script made 23-24 scorecards:get reads plus one plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy call. An identical retry succeeded both times. Afterwards the responses carried _dataPlaneMayBeDegraded warnings. A testing:runs error at ~02:13Z said build d740fc3802 had 'started 25min ago'. The scorecards:emit response at 02:16:10Z reported gradedGeneration.hostStartedAt=2026-10-13T02:14:09Z and staleHost=true. So the serving host apparently restarted between 02:13 and 02:14:09. That restart came AFTER both resets, so a restart does not obviously explain them.

Why it matters: outcome_unknown on a code:run means the caller cannot tell whether nested writes happened, so every agent has to reason about idempotency on each reset. A read-only audit can safely retry; a writing script cannot.

Probe: query harness_shared.tool_invocations for coord_owner_id su-628f4d8c-87ea-4d57-a493-58504e273aa3, tool_name code:run, between 02:10 and 02:13Z, and read serving_host / serving_build_sha / duration. Correlate that with the :9071 proxy log for the two traceIds and the operator journal for that window. Check whether long-running code:run (~25 nested dispatches) is hitting an upstream socket or idle timeout.

Together these connect unavailable host attachment to blocked forced recovery and a persistent limit breach. The shared repair boundary is managed-host resolution/attachment or supported hostless compaction; why hosts became unavailable is not established. Unpaired over-limit and dark-telemetry alarms are excluded.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
UNCONFIRMED. The root cause is not known; the timing link below is an inference.

Observed 2026-10-14 ~07:06-07:08Z by the grading-integrity judge (audit EI-25937822279694569 of card EI-25937267761663359). I made the same read three times: plans:get-spec-evidence { harness:'papercusp', slug:'consult-backed-parking-2026-10-12', specIds:['AUTO-BAR-R-21-P-007'], detail:'full' } (bindings 43554, 43555).
- Call 1 (code:run callId ubrxmz-k8x, elapsedMs 6208): both bindings returned currentness {"overall":"unknown","dimensions":{"spec":"current","source":"unknown","test":"unknown","fixture":…}. The output was truncated, and I did not capture unknownReasons.
- Call 2 (~1 min later): top-level currentness {current:2, stale:0, unknown:0}.
- Call 3 (callId ubrxmz-kbx, elapsedMs 111): both bindings overall:current, every dimension current, provenance server-measured, no stale/unknown reasons.
Nothing about the bindings changed in between (createdAt 06:57:11/12Z, no retraction).

Why it matters: a grader or auditor who takes the slow read reports freshness 'unknown' on proof that is current, so currentness is a function of server load rather than evidence. That is a false negative from a measuring instrument.

Hypothesis [inferred, not probed]: under load the server-side source/test fingerprint measurement times out or degrades to 'unknown' instead of retrying or surfacing a load reason. Probe: re-run the read while the operator is under concurrent load and compare currentness.unknownReasons with the elapsedMs of the same call. If the reason is a timeout or deadline, the unknown is load-induced and should carry a distinct reason such as measurement-deadline, not read as evidence-unknown.

Related (different tool, same class): EI-25931455671559212 (scorecards:get transient rubricCurrentness unknown under concurrent load). Result-door spill ETIMEDOUT also recurred about 8 times in this audit session (already filed as EI-25932014678052487).

Disposition requested: treat this filing as historical transport friction with existing recovery guidance, rather than an implementation-ready current product defect. A renewed defect claim would need trace-correlated same-key recovery failure or evidence the persisted conversation/result was lost. No code changes, recovery-success claim, or universal absence claim.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Suspected recurring transient MCP proxy transport failure; diagnosis remains unconfirmed.

Observed source invocation: backup:snapshot_list (read-only) was called through tools:invoke and returned HTTP 502 mcp_proxy_upstream_error after connecting; detail read ECONNRESET; forwardingResult=outcome_unknown. Because the forwarding result is unknown, this record cannot establish whether the backup handler completed or whether snapshot state changed; no snapshot ID or terminal snapshot state was returned.

Independent corroboration: a distinct reporter recorded the same backup:snapshot_list 502/ECONNRESET/outcome_unknown signature at 2026-10-15T01:14:08.525Z, and the capture promotion path merged it into this item. This repeats the transport symptom; it does not independently identify its cause. The stored class is transient, runtime/schema are unknown, and no successful reproduction is recorded.

Scope exclusions: EI-25470369376845808 was a separate MCP_RESULT_TIMEOUT on the direct endpoint, and EI-25641774268364729 is a separate snapshot_create timeout. Neither validates this reset or establishes backup state.

Action: keep this open as a promoted suspected proxy transport defect. Before diagnosing or fixing it, correlate both events with proxy/upstream logs or trace identifiers, or reproduce through the same route while recording the serving runtime and terminal outcome. Do not infer snapshot state or claim a root cause from these reports alone.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-10-21 (su-2b61b6ab, audit WI-6554700010019485):
- bg-host journal: "[scheduled-registry] ephemeral:rt_papercusp_acceptance_grading_sweep long tick finished after 2557003ms (42 fire(s) skipped while it ran, interval 60000ms)" at 18:49:08Z.
- the bg-host restarted ~18:56Z; the new tick has been "still running" since (log lines at 120 s, 253 s, 982 s, 1,944 s). schedule:inventory (bg-host:3271) shows fires=0, running=true, armedAt 18:56:35Z.
- routines row rt_papercusp_acceptance_grading_sweep: active, last_fired_at 18:49:08Z.

EFFECT: a 60 s sweep that re-dispatches graders and mints escalations effectively runs once per ~40 min, and a bg-host restart mid-tick discards the whole pass. The registry logs "still running" but nothing alarms or bounds the tick, so a hung tick stops the cadence silently until the next restart.

ROOT CAUSE: NOT established; which await inside the action (harness/routines/acceptance-grading-sweep-action.ts and acceptance-grading-sweep-run.ts) takes the time was not measured. Related: EI-26281797513320642 (hypothesis about lastFiredAt not advancing).

FIX DIRECTION: keep the scan on the ephemeral timer but cap its wall time, and run each per-plan dispatch as a DBOS workflow keyed by plan + gradeable-since, so the tick finishes in seconds and dispatches survive restarts. Add an alarm when a managed tick holds its guard past N intervals.

Valid capability:launch-agent resume session01a164ab-69c9-78f1-b027-4d89965018f9, fork:false/headless/default/gpt-6.1-sol:xhigh opened0/failed1. Source launch-agent.ts pre-pins in-place resume target to original ended owner and passes owner:targetOwnerId into spawnGovernedAgentProcess; admission-ledger-store reconciliation legitimately reclaims that ended owner's lease before any process can revive it. This is a launch lifecycle/admission ordering defect, not a reason to weaken ended-owner reclamation or fake principal liveness. Recurrence test must exercise ended source + live authorized launcher, prove exact-identity governed start, and retain post-start owner-death/expiry protection. Operational mitigation: replace the stopped implementation worker with a fresh governed member of the same fleet and transfer original claims; keep this bug open/owned until durable fix and meaningful regression proof. _claimSubjectBaseline.body: Unconfirmed suspected tool responsiveness bug. On 2026-10-23, ptool calls to dev:pg_health (localOnly) and dev:telemetry both ended with transport Request timed out after 30.003s and 30.004s, with execution outcome unknown. A bounded dev:pg_hot_queries sample (windowSec=5) did return, but only after the nested command had yielded past 30s. A subsequent tools:find through proxy 127.0.0.1:9171 failed after 25.959s with proxy-upstream-502; its unverified local-direct fallback was correctly refused. Repeating tools:find with --url=http://localhost:3170 then succeeded through the proxy in 2.345s. Cause is unknown; this does not establish DB execution delay or fleet load as the cause. Diagnose by correlating ptool request IDs, proxy dispatch, and operator response timing.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-26 ~19:55Z (su-96b7fe62). Under load, every operator-core testing:run hits the ~40s foreground cap and returns { ok:false, error:'timeout', runId, detachedRunId, ... }. I projected `runId` (the obvious name) and passed it to testing:run-status. All 5 calls returned unknown_run ('may be unknown or evicted ... not evidence that the test passed'), although the runs were alive. Only `detachedRunId` resolves. Example: runId 20528708-c2dc-4881-8c87-f5c055eb7878 -> unknown_run; the later call's detachedRunId 7a4f9a99-... resolved. Fix: make testing:run-status accept the foreground runId and resolve it to its detached run (or alias them), or drop runId from the timeout result. The unknown_run message should also say 'did you pass runId instead of detachedRunId?'.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 ~00:06Z (su-fc263bb4). The work_items:claim concurrencyWarning text says: raise the cap deliberately with scheduler:set_claim_spec { limits: { maxConcurrentClaims: N } }. The live schema refuses `limits` at the top level (accepts clear, confirmCollapse, confirmGoalFenceDrop, cupId, fleet, harness, spec). Nesting it as spec:{limits:{...}} is refused too, because spec requires specVersion, specId, revision, view and rank. So the advice cannot be followed as written. Fix: change the warning to name a working call (for example read the current spec and resubmit it with only limits changed, or add a partial-update arg such as maxConcurrentClaims to set_claim_spec), and pin the warning text with a test that runs its prescribed call through schema validation.

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools` (12202 newer commits, tip `41c6812d7813b8b0f62fc6594615c778bf48d7c2`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

Possible fix: have tools:invoke accept a JSON-string args and parse it (the error already knows the corrected shape), instead of refusing.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 02:10Z (su-ad3061a6, owner directive #2375 agent recovery).

Evidence:
- `harness_shared.task_ledger` GROUP BY workspace_id,state (updated_at > now()-3d): papercusp-workspace rows are reconciled continuously (running/exited/ended_unobserved updated to 02:10Z). workspace_id='default' has 14 rows in state='running' whose newest last_seen_at is 2026-10-26 04:12Z and oldest 2026-10-24 02:18Z — never touched since insertion.
- Example: task 0mvmvat7w12xrl4v10z (class agent-session, title 'headless member: successor · su-16e3554c-…', fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-0930, scope pc-0mvmvat7w12xrl4v10z--successor-su-16e3554c-….scope). `processes:kill { taskId }` returns already_gone (systemd no longer knows the scope), yet the row still reads running / ended_at NULL / last_seen_at 2026-10-24 20:44:51Z.

Mechanism (from source, unverified beyond reading): `task-reconcile` system action → `reconcileTick({ workspaceId: deps.workspaceId })` → `listLiveTasks(workspaceId)` → `listTasks({ workspaceId, states:['pending','running'] })` (packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/store.ts:1194, reconcile-tick.ts:192). The routine runs per install with ctx.workspaceId='papercusp-workspace', so rows written under workspace_id='default' are outside every reconcile population. cgroups are host-global, so the host's reconciler should own every row on this host regardless of workspace tag.

Impact: a never-terminal 'running' row is false liveness evidence. `capability:launch-agent { successor }` for su-16e3554c refused 'predecessor liveness is live/draining; positive terminal evidence is required' while the process was gone; that agent stayed wedged on stale-artifact (29 authorization_denied, 0 ok, last 01:54Z).

Proposed fix: (1) reconcile ALL workspaces' pending/running rows whose scope_unit/cgroup is on this host (or explicitly include 'default'); (2) find the writer that records workspace_id='default' for headless fleet-member launches (managedSpawn/enroll called without an active workspace — 10-24 headless member successor launches) and pass the real workspace; (3) killTask: when a live-owned row's scope resolves already_gone, record the terminal transition (ended_unobserved, reason scope-collected) instead of returning without updating the ledger. Recurrence guard: a reconcile-tick test that seeds a running row under a different workspace_id with a collected scope and asserts it is transitioned.

Related (distinct symptom, same subsystem): EI-26986308927850569 / EI-26993855168505100 / EI-26991528350067840 (rt_papercusp_task_reconcile 'hung' alarms).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 on consult conv-mvq2vlgs-0000-eebfb91af52c405a8ae7d3b9c53ed149 (decision-review for EI-25927909729992864).

Timeline (all UTC, from conversations:get payloadTier:'full' + my own launch stamp):
- 03:02:39.334 reviewer 1 (su-2a8dbdd0) posts answer 1207631 → per D-005 the cascade ADVANCES and launches reviewer 2/2.
- ~03:02:59 reviewer 2 (this session, su-ec58d1ae) boots on a ported codex transcript (session-port 7946addc-68e4-4209-af56-48d392f3551c, fidelity: full — a full context carry).
- 03:03:11.213 reviewer 1 posts close 1207633 → consult.state = closed_answered.
- 03:05 reviewer 2 finishes reading the thread + grounding evidence and calls consult:reply { kind:'answer', stance:{position:'support'} } → refused: {"error":"consult_not_open","state":"closed_answered"}.

Net: an entire reviewer session launch (full-fidelity transcript port + ~15 tool calls of evidence reading) produced nothing deliverable, and the launch brief told reviewer 2 it was 'launched to answer ONE question' with no indication the thread could already be terminal.

Three plausible fixes (any one suffices; first is cheapest):
1. consult:close (and any terminal transition) should CANCEL an in-flight reviewer dispatch for that conversation if that reviewer has not yet posted — the launch is attributable (dispatch.recent walks), so the close handler can mark it cancelled and the wake-executor can skip/abort the boot.
2. The reviewer launch brief / first wake should re-check consult.state before spending the transcript port; if state is terminal, deliver a one-line 'already closed — stand down' instead of the full answer brief (saves the boot cost even when fix 1 misses the race).
3. When a reviewer's reply is immediately followed by its own close (same author, < N seconds), do not advance the cascade on the reply — treat reply+close as one atomic 'answer and settle' and never launch the next reviewer. (D-005 'reply advances' is correct when the replier does NOT close.)

Also worth noting: consult:reply on a closed thread returns a bare consult_not_open with no pointer to the accepted answer; a hint naming accepted_post_id would let a stranded reviewer confirm concurrence cheaply instead of re-reading.

Evidence: conversations:get conv-mvq2vlgs-0000-eebfb91af52c405a8ae7d3b9c53ed149 (consult.state, closed_at, posts 1207631/1207633 timestamps); the refused consult:reply invocation by su-ec58d1ae-58c7-4c7a-88ce-8a479bb0f29c at ~03:05Z in harness_shared.tool_invocations. Related but distinct: EI-27099846407216760 (duplicate consult minted by idempotent park replay) — that one spends a THIRD reviewer on the orphan; this one spends reviewer 2 on the live thread.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Root cause class (measured on EI-27114233692780034): Postgres jsonb stores object keys ordered by length then bytes, so JSON.stringify(readBack) !== JSON.stringify(inMemory) for logically equal objects. That orphaned every measured R6 admission precheck. Fixed there with canonicalJson from @papercusp/hash-chain.

Remaining candidate sites (grep `JSON.stringify(...) [!=]== JSON.stringify` over release/, agent-tools/release/, harness/routines/, excluding tests), each needing a check of whether either side is a jsonb read-back:
- packages/operator-core/lib/release/checkpoint-qualification-transaction.ts:730 (prior.retryStates vs retryStates) and :1610 (current.eligibilitySnapshot vs parsed)
- packages/operator-core/lib/release/gate-hygiene-split.ts:758 (current[key] vs replay.expected[key])
- packages/operator-core/lib/release/checkpoint-serializer-authority.ts:108 (priorTransition.prerequisiteWorkItems)
- packages/operator-core/lib/release/checkpoint-eligibility-snapshot.ts:199-201 (parsed vs row predicates/blockers/safeNextAction)
- packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/release-actions.ts:6765 (persisted.rows vs manifest rows; a false mismatch would set statusChanged every tick)
- packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/template-gym-runner.ts:120,133,257

Fix: replace each object-valued comparison with canonicalJson(a) === canonicalJson(b) (or isDeepStrictEqual where key order is irrelevant). Arrays of scalars are safe as-is. Durable guard: a lint (shrink-only baseline) flagging `JSON.stringify(x) ===/!== JSON.stringify(y)` in operator-core non-test code, plus one jsonb round-trip regression test per fixed site.

Observed 2026-10-27T18:14Z: `systemctl --user show papercusp-vm-mac.service` returns ActiveState=failed, SubState=failed, Result=exit-code, MainPID=0, InactiveEnterTimestamp=Sat 2026-10-24 09:59 EDT, UnitFileState=enabled. The unit's journal had no entries in this probe, so the cause of the exit is UNKNOWN.

Impact: packages/operator-core/lib/storage/final-disk-accounting.live.test.ts enables itself when the VM dirs exist, not when the VM is running. Its case 'keeps both relocations healthy and the macOS VM running from backup storage' fails with 8 VM violations, so it is a frozen-lineage red (see WI-6554700010030395 comment 1208361). The relocation and audit-archive checks pass.

There are two issues: (1) the VM unit failed and was never restarted. Restart=? If it is supposed to stay up, it needs restart or supervision. (2) Detector: a host service in failed state for 3+ days did not visibly page anyone. Check whether papercusp-vm-mac is covered by the supervision registry and the unregistered-failed-unit census. Note that the census's unit test is also red because of drift (same WI comment, item 2), so the census path may be under-tested.

Proposed: decide whether the VM must be up. If yes, restart it, find the exit cause, and add supervision. If no, make the live test assert relocation only when the VM is intentionally off, by an explicit marker and not by loosening.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-27 (su-fc263bb4, papercusp install). The git-sync activity row showed one fire (started_at 18:59:09Z, phase local-sync) running until about 19:19Z. During that fire it ran `git status` in papercusp-desktop for 80s+ and then pushed that submodule. Its commit 5e6605dc3b (19:19:26Z) contained only test-config and the papercusp-desktop gitlink. The fire's last_content_errors still list push-channel.ts, task-brief.ts and task-brief.test.ts as quarantined importers of push-toolset.ts, 'held by su-fc263bb4 — turn-scoped hold: edited during its editor's current turn'. That editor's turns ended at about 19:06Z and again at about 19:20Z. No commit landed between 18:44Z and 19:19Z: freshness reported 9 missed intervals and the scheduler was 'stalled_behind_in_flight_fire'. Meanwhile the infra-liveness condition git-sync-missed-intervals:papercusp kept broadcasting RECOVERED while freshness still said degraded.

Suspected (unconfirmed): the turn-scoped hold set is evaluated once near the start of a fire and not re-checked at commit time, so a slow fire commits against a stale hold list. Separately, one fire spending 20 minutes in local-sync (a submodule `git status` taking 80s+) blocks every agent's commits for that whole period. The repeated RECOVERED broadcasts while freshness says degraded look like a false recovery signal.

Evidence: routines:list { name:'git-sync', installSlug:'papercusp' } health.git_sync_activity / git_sync_freshness / last_content_errors, read at 19:12Z, 19:15Z and 19:20Z; `git log` shows d47a64ee2f at 18:44:11Z, then 5e6605dc3b at 19:19:26Z.

Proposed fix: re-check turn-scoped holds right before staging each repo's commit, not once per fire. Bound how long the local-sync phase may run per submodule. Make the infra-liveness RECOVERED broadcast agree with git_sync_freshness.status.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-28 ~02:12Z (su-76dc3403, owner directive #2536). Resumed 14 ended su agents with capability:launch-agent { agent:'claude', resume:{ agentId }, fork:false, brief, idempotencyKey } (7 in parallel via code:run). For 3 of them (su-96b7fe62, su-fe99c651, su-2fde89b1) the result had no resumeVerification/resumeVerified, and each original identity came up on a NEW native session id (9fab66ac / 2b6a3bc1 / bda1c09f). Two extra sessions then appeared with launch_parent_owner = me, started 22:12:50 ET, argv `psu --no-picker --resume=<that new sid> --fork --agent=claude ...`: su-35233845 (fork of su-fe99c651 sid 2b6a3bc1; it detected the duplicate and stood down) and su-5f692bae (fork of su-2fde89b1 sid bda1c09f). Contract per the arg doc: `fork:false requires non-live in-place recovery` and refuses a live source, so no --fork launch should ever come from a fork:false call. Unconfirmed mechanism [inferred]: the source turned live mid-call (a system revive/wake-executor or the first in-place launch registering), and some path such as a retry, a second attempt or an auto-fork-on-live branch ignored fork:false. Evidence: harness_shared.adv_sessions rows for su-35233845 / su-5f692bae (launch_argv), plus the code:run batch output. Fix: thread fork:false through every retry/live-source branch so it refuses (typed error) instead of forking; also return resumeVerification on every resume result.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed by su-96b7fe62 (gate owner WI-10006055) on 2026-10-28. A release:repair-queue {op:'admit', confirm:true, 149 paths, wholeBlob@969ae43a} sent via mcp-call --port 3170 at 11:10:22Z returned MCP request_timeout ("exceeded 300000ms, commit status is UNKNOWN") at 11:15:24Z. tool_invocations id 45515599 shows the server finished in 305063ms with a complete answer: refused admission-incomplete 0b51b3bb3434 with 32 missing refs. timings.steps build-proof = 275187ms. The answer existed only in the output_ref scratch spill. The caller had to reconstruct it by hand: dev:pg_query on tool_invocations, then parse a 400KB scratch file. A naive agent would blind-retry (risking a double apply) or wait.

Proposed fix: make admit confirm an async operation like admission previews. Return {operationId} immediately and emit release:repair-queue:admit-settled:<id> carrying verdict/missing/movedRepairHead, so callers events:await instead of holding a 5-min request. Alternatively, give release:repair-queue a per-tool timeout above the build-proof ceiling. Separately, the dry-run path caps build-proof at 240s (ADMISSION_PREVIEW_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS, repair-queue.ts:208), so a large set can never get a dry-run answer under load (related: EI-27221310811396187). Host load at the time: ~150 on 128 cores, PG IO-bound (EI-27221039154567484).

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/repair-queue.ts` (101 newer commits, tip `06332a9467f5983dfd63aecf06c4afbbaee05f89`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Seen 2026-10-28 ~14:41Z by su-a835dc70 during WI-6554700010042405 / owner directive #2561. 13 Codex agents were relaunched over about 3 minutes via capability:launch-agent resume with account:'auto'. Two headless launches died at boot with exit 78. Their psu log (.papercusp/fleet-logs/relaunch-su-respawn-404-373010-1793198468736.log) says: "REFUSING TO LAUNCH — Codex auto-route has no serviceable accounts: 0 of 8; earliest known recovery 2026-10-28T14:41:22.806Z". Visible launches in the same burst then logged launch-kickoff-model-turn-absent (su-8257d540, su-4bdf29dd) and native-turn-failed (su-3d698393 at 14:42:06Z). At the same time, accounts:list { provider:'codex' } showed rate.history7d utilization of 0.02-0.16 on 7 of 8 accounts; only aviynw_codex (free plan) was at u=1. Cause UNCONFIRMED. Possibilities: a burst of concurrent Codex starts tripped per-account/edge exclusions, OR the snapshot was stale. Either way, a mass relaunch produces dead sessions without telling the launcher. Suggested: launch-agent should fail fast (before opening a window) when the route snapshot is walled, and the gateway should explain WHY each account was excluded.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Code-confirmed integration gap discovered during owner-requested architectural assessment. dependency-staleness.ts observeCell() takes status:value reads and hashes only read.value, optionally read.material.value; CurrentCellObservation has no assessment code/status, evidence digest, source-authoritativeness, or unknownHoist. evaluateDependencyStaleness() returns fresh when headline/material digests match. By contrast state:subscribe defaults to assessment changes. Concrete case: git.pipelinePosition headline is positions.deployed; both live and restart-required can have true, while assessment changes based on serving.startedSinceCodeChange. Even more directly, a read may keep status:value and unchanged headline while assessment becomes unavailable; freshness still hashes that value and can report fresh. No production incident claimed; mechanism established by source. Proposed fix: extend existing FactDependency/CurrentCellObservation with a versioned assessment/status anchor (and necessary measuredness/source qualifiers), capture from the same read, and mark semantic changes stale or unassessable readings undeterminable. Preserve explicit materiality semantics. Add canonical regression tests for same measurement/different assessment and assessment unavailable. Existing tests cover raw/material drift but have no assessment cases (rg assessment|semantic over dependency-staleness.ts and its test).

Host mandatory checkpoint snapshot repeatedly fails PG57014 statement_timeout at P005 WI-6554700010025564, fingerprint6385e22c033dbd7e. Most recent source audit found bounded row-lock read + carry_notes INSERT/ON CONFLICT path; no source defect proven. During the outstanding checkpoint write (toolkey76909000-df94-4058-ad9f-9cffba024995, subsequently verified landed as primary checkpoint2ac63795e9c6), bounded dev:pg_query sample via code:run dispatch z24lih-gz measured five active carry_notes statements: PID2644058 insert-upsert age49.915876s waiting IO/WalSync, blockers[]; PID1868378 insert-upsert age46.958218s waiting LWLock/tapir_memtable_write_lock, blockers[]; PID50948 other carry_notes statement age46.950796s same LWLock; PID3392549 insert-upsert25.670889s same LWLock; PID2434457 insert-upsert18.034869s same LWLock. This establishes write-path waiting, not a row-lock blocker or proof that generic CPU/RAM/load causes it. Root cause of slow WAL durability or Tapir lock hold remains unknown. Investigate the WAL-sync holder and Tapir lock serialization with bounded IO/engine evidence; add recurrence detection that attributes prolonged carry-note write waits, and enrich host checkpoint timeout diagnosis with actual wait stage. Preserve durability; do not disable fsync, skip mandatory checkpointing, restart PostgreSQL, or widen deadlines as a substitute for root repair. Exact existing dedup search tapir_memtable_write_lock was attempted once and rejected superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable, so duplicate coverage is unknown.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed while authoring the WI2457 eight-bar amendment on current3170: a single custody predicate, 'Qualification custody remains held for every enumerated mutation while any enrolled managed scope is live or unknown, regardless of DBOS age or absent completed-step output, under the retained explicit operator and scoped-operation authorities', was refused with acceptance_bar_non_atomic_projection / joins multiple independently observable outcomes. Direct source diagnosis: agent-tools/plans/spec-clause-compiler.ts ADDITIONAL_OBSERVABLE_VERB includes complet(?:e|es|ed|ing), MULTI_EXTENDED_CONJUNCTION_RE spans 'remains ... or ... completed', and ATTRIBUTIVE_PARTICIPLE_RE does not normalize the noun modifier in 'absent completed-step output'. This is a false-positive atomicity finding; replacing it with semantically equivalent 'missing operation-output evidence' made the preview pass. Durable proposed fix: recognize completed-step / completion-output noun modifiers in the predicate normalization, with maintained positive/negative tests so real coordinated completion predicates still fail. Keep the gate strict; do not broadly disable compound-outcome validation. Native dry-run receipts are in this SAME598a1 continuation before preview1215966; final valid amendment D006/approval1215989 is unrelated to implementation acceptance. Filing this additional source diagnosis rather than duplicating a plain tool error.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Additional diagnosis beyond automatically recorded tool timeouts. After exact Restart/apps same-inode bind repair and maintained SSR guard23698031 PASS, normal locks:release b6880c6a-41e1-47a0-acc1-589916b6cce2 failed twice; tool_invocations48149791/48150126 store write CONNECTION_CLOSED localhost:5432 after109024/123338ms. Their ledger status='ok' is not release success. Readback still holds three edited paths plus apps parent and external rollback path. CLI idempotency key6b30fbd3-cc7e-4c31-8167-6561b73202b3; original and same-key replay55s dispatch timeouts were not blindly retried. Source inspection: release.ts409-415 executes preserveReleasedEditGenerations inside tryRelease/inWorkspaceTxn before release. edit-attribution.ts563+ groups rows and awaits Git capture/readback then separate org-ledger attribution. SU database default idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s verified via dev:pg_query pg_db_role_setting; su-lock-store.ts342 sets30s. Hypothesis: callback spends >30s out of SQL while preserving source generations, SU backend expires and release cannot commit. Alternative connection cause not ruled out until PostgreSQL log correlation/test. Plausible durable fix: preserve version/fence guarantees while keeping bounded transaction lifetime; avoid holding an idle SQL transaction across arbitrarily long filesystem/Git capture (reuse existing protected operation/custody receipt), or explicit maintained long-transaction liveness if already supported. Add maintained integration detector with short PG idle timeout and delayed capture, asserting preserved bytes, release success and rollback/failedcapture stays held. Do not weaken custody, force release, disable global GUC, or merely widen timeouts. Current task needs safe normal release; investigate narrow per-group normal release using existing immutable capture receipts only after authoritative failed-outcome/held-state read. Relevant logs: f700-post-bind-release-20261109.err, -release-replay-.err; own source/app bytes remain unchanged.
