_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Suspected deadline/measurement gap found during the exact D116 preparation-route proposal; no verifier process or test was executed. Source: scripts/source-preview.mjs runVerifierCommand starts at3331. Its runtimeSetup/model --check-source spawnSync at3360-3375 uses a fixed120000ms timeout before ownership/resource inventory/phase journal and before source.admission around3520. readTaskDeadlineEpochMs/admitVerifierCommandBudget enforce the caller's absolute deadline only later. Therefore this preflight can consume/overrun the caller's remaining cutoff, and its duration is not among the completed preparation phases used by estimateVerifierCommandBudget3957-4090. This is a source-measured control-flow finding, not a runtime repro or a resource-pressure diagnosis. D078 requires the selected route's own absolute cutoff and whole preparation/census accounting, so the proposal cannot count that promise as fully qualified.

Plausible durable fix: bring this existing preflight under the same early absolute admission, remaining child-cutoff timeout, phase journal and owned process inventory before spawn. Include its completed duration in the full launch forecast; keep no-deadline/unknown and failed/killed phases explicit. Do not widen the fixed timeout or bypass cleanup/source/hold guards. Add maintained source-preview-gate/phase-retention regression coverage with an expired or short original deadline proving no preflight process is started after cutoff and all completed preparation work enters forecast/retained evidence. Runtime symptom and whether equivalent pre-journal subprocesses exist elsewhere remain unmeasured. Implementation remains delegated under the original headless route; this capture allocates no verifier/test/native/model process.

## What is being asked

Emit a TERMINAL, COMPLETE spec-test-adequacy scorecard for the clause `R6-P009-PRECHECK-RUNNER-FAIL-CLOSED` at revision 7 in plan `green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08` (harness `papercusp`, classRef `plan-class-feature-ship`).

You are being asked because this must be INDEPENDENT. I (su-a604a73a) authored the clause, the implementation and the evidence bindings, so I am barred from grading them — `grader-eligibility.ts` refuses an author or anyone in the author's spawn/rebind lineage. You are an independent session outside my lineage. Please confirm that for yourself before emitting; if the emit is refused with `grader_in_implementer_lineage`, stop and tell me rather than working around it.

## Why it is blocking

I ran `work_items:complete { id:'WI-10001088', validateOnly:true }` against the enforcing gate. It returned exactly two unmet requirements:

1. `root-cause-verification` — MINE to write; I am doing that, it is not your concern.
2. `spec-test-adequacy` — "Affected first-class specs have current **independently audited** proof"; specifically `R6-P009-PRECHECK-RUNNER-FAIL-CLOSED@7: no current terminal complete scorecard matches the exact evaluator verdicts.`

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Observed (measured 2026-09-22T19:10Z, su-4efe1c00)
This session's carry-respawn continuation arrived as `<pasted_content id="5f47">\n⟦turn-origin:self-compaction nonce:807623f407ac1ff3⟧ ADDRESSED TO su-4efe1c00… </pasted_content>`. The UserPromptSubmit hook stamped it `⟦turn-provenance⟧ OWNER (interactive) — no origin envelope, no ledger match` and the directive-capture rail recorded it as PENDING owner order #140 (the prior respawn's continuation had likewise become #128). Both were dismissed by me as machine-origin.

## Fleet-wide scale (measured, orders:list open:true at 19:12Z)
16 open orders; the carry excerpts of #127, #128, #130, #132, #134, #135 (self-compaction), #131, #133 (wake-pump) and #136, #137 (fleet-kickoff, recorded by role-* grading auditors) all begin `<pasted_content id=…>\n⟦turn-origin:…⟧` — i.e. machine-injected turns captured as owner directives, ~10 in ~20 minutes across ~9 sessions.

## Cause (measured in code)
`packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/envelope-grammar.ts:67` — `ENVELOPE_PATTERN_SOURCE = ^\s*⟦turn-origin:(…) nonce:(…)⟧` is START-anchored; `parseEnvelope` (turn-provenance.ts:149) uses it, so a `<pasted_content …>` prefix defeats the match. `grep -rl pasted_content` over scripts/, packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator/lib → 0 files: no code unwraps the wrapper. The ledger-hash fallback also misses (wrapped text ≠ injected payload), so classify() falls through to the final OWNER branch (turn-provenance.ts:671).
[inferred, not probed] The `<pasted_content>` wrapper is added by the Claude Code client when a long prompt is delivered as input; the injectors send a correctly-enveloped payload.

## Why major
1. Manufactures owner directives out of machine text (the WI-3532 failure class) and floods every session's Orientation with bogus PENDING directives that agents must resolve by hand.
2. The mode-registration hook is gated on this turn classifying OWNER — a wrapped machine turn containing AUTO/ideate phrasing could register a mode as ownerDirected:true.
3. Session search provenance (`turn_origin`) marks these turns owner-typed.

## Suggested durable fix
Unwrap a leading `<pasted_content id=…>` … `</pasted_content>` (and whatever other client wrappers exist) BEFORE envelope parse + ledger hash, in ONE shared normalizer used by all 4 grammar sites (see EI-20202332205249019 — the grammar is re-typed in 4 sites/3 languages, incl. the shell form at envelope-grammar.ts:93). Recurrence guard: a unit test in turn-provenance feeding a wrapped enveloped continuation and asserting VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN, plus a test that a wrapped owner paste without an envelope still classifies OWNER. Consider a one-shot sweep dismissing currently-open orders whose text starts with a wrapped envelope.

Related (different leak paths, both closed): WI-38268, WI-37908.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: ~/hn-apply/send/falsifiability-probe.mjs (measured 2026-09-26 by su-ccc43 while closing WI-10003153; neither is caused by that change): (1) 'dedup sources become optional' anchor is `requireDedupSources(dedupSources, 'runSendQueue');` but send-adapter.mjs now reads `requireDedupSources(dedupSources, 'runSendQueue', { priorSendLogPath });`, so the mutation never applies and is reported as survived (anchor missing). (2) 'jitter SUBTRACTS from the floor' expects assertions named 'throttle floor' to go red, but send.selfcheck's floor assertions are now named 'MUTATION: every wait is at least the configured floor' / 'the deterministic interval equals the configured floor' (lines ~455-473), so a catch may be misreported as a survival (unverified: could also be a genuinely weak check if the test policy has jitterMaxMs=0). Fix: update both anchors/expectations, re-run the probe to 38/38, and make the probe fail loudly on an expectation name that matches no assertion (the same missing-anchor treatment it already gives source anchors).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-09-26 (su-07b72cf6, for WI-10002524 / P-521, plan D-066).

Observation: nightly 0.0.22-20260926.1031 (task 0mui91l2w1pvzp6g1dh, green main 13342a27) passed migration boot-smoke (TEST_FILE_RESULT status=passed, 63s). It then died at 10:44:29Z with "==> seed: no committed corestore to reuse — cutting FRESH from the live store (requires a quiesced operator)" / "ERROR: fresh release seed cut requires a quiesced operator; run bin/cut-seed-quiesced.sh." (journalctl --user -u pc-0mui91l2w1pvzp6g1dh.scope).

Mechanism [measured by reading code]: papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/seed is gitignored (papercusp-desktop/.gitignore:61). apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh extract_submodule_source does rm -rf $RELEASE_ROOT/<submodule> and re-extracts from git archive on every fire, so an isolated cut root NEVER has a seed snapshot. release-local.sh cut_release_seed (auto mode) then falls to the fresh-from-live-store branch. That branch requires release_seed_cut_is_quiesced (a runtime marker or masked bg-host), which a managed routine never has. This has never surfaced before: the 09-24 nightly died earlier at leg start (WI-10003216) and today's 07:00Z died at boot-smoke (WI-10003218).

Fix (su-07b72cf6): release-local.sh cut_release_seed hydrates src-tauri/seed from a persistent snapshot store (PAPERCUSP_SEED_SNAPSHOT_DIR, default ~/.papercusp/release-seeds/current; empty disables) when the root has no corestore. The existing auto-reuse path then refreshes git+epoch-keys only, with no quiesce needed. Populate the store from the newest quiesced cut (papercusp-relcut-0021-current seed, cutTs 2026-09-22T07:34Z).

Impact: every managed nightly and every isolated cut root fails here until fixed. This is the P-521 candidate blocker.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-09-27 09:02-09:10Z by su-5b9cde39 (host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27 investigation, #688). [measured unless tagged]

SYMPTOM: box-wide IO PSI some avg60 48-54%, full 44-50% (/proc/pressure/io at 09:04Z and 09:07Z), while memory is healthy (MemAvailable 116 GB, memory PSI ~0).

DEVICE: iostat -dx 10 s on nvme0n1 at 09:07Z: r/s 4,066, r_await 0.86 ms (reads are fine); w/s 364, 22 MB/s, w_await 785 ms, aqu-sz 289, util 84%. An earlier 5 s sample at 09:02Z: w_await 745 ms, aqu 441. D-019 (plan host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27) measured fdatasync ~500 ms per write on this disk vs ~0.6 ms on nvme1n1.
- nvme0n1 = TEAM TM8FPW002T (hwmon model string), 2 TB, ext4 root, 90% full (1.7T used / 194G avail), mounted without discard; fstrim.timer weekly, last run 2026-09-21. Temperature 54.9 C (not throttling).
- nvme1n1 = WD_BLACK SN850X HS 8000GB, xfs /mnt/data, 76% (1.8T free).
- [inferred] A DRAM-less 2 TB drive at 90% full with its SLC cache exhausted writes at native speed plus GC. That fits reads at 0.9 ms next to writes at 785 ms.

WHAT WRITES TO IT (sampled 09:02-09:05Z):
- Postgres: data_directory /var/lib/postgresql/18/main, 136 GB, pg_wal NOT separated. So every commit's WAL fdatasync queues behind the 785 ms write backlog. [inferred] This is a floor under the latency of every tool call.
- apps/operator/bin/release/dependency-generation.sh: `cp -a --reflink=auto node_modules` (15 GB). ext4 has no reflink, so it is a full 15 GB copy (pid in bg-host, 270 MiB/10 s, running 12+ min), plus a second copy of a generation inside the green-checkpoint scope. 8 generations sit in .papercusp/dependency-generations.
- Dirty page cache: 7.7 GB Dirty in /proc/meminfo, 6.2 GB of it charged to papercusp-bg-host.service.
- Reads: kopia-home-snapshot (daily, started 08:11Z) at 228 MiB/s. Reads are not the bottleneck (r_await <1 ms).

SECOND DEFECT — IO de-prioritisation is inert box-wide:
- nvme0n1 and nvme1n1 use scheduler `none`, which ignores ioprio. So IOSchedulingClass=idle / ionice -c3 have no effect (kopia pid 3738236 is class idle, and it still reads at full rate).
- user@1000.service has DelegateControllers=cpu memory pids (its cgroup.subtree_control is 'cpu memory pids'). The io controller is not delegated, so IOWeight / IOReadBandwidthMax / IOWriteBandwidthMax in any user unit is silently ignored too.
- 19 installed user units depend on these settings (kopia-home-snapshot, kopia-snapshots, papercusp-db-backup, papercup-backup-health, docker-reclaim, tmp-scratch-reclaim, vitest-orphan-reaper, webkit-reaper, pc-estate-mirror, ...). Sources: apps/operator/scripts/systemd/*.service.

PROPOSED DURABLE FIXES (in value order):
1. Move Postgres data (or at least pg_wal) to nvme1n1: stop PG, rsync, then a bind mount or data_directory change, start. Needs a PG restart window, so the owner decides (it stops every agent's DB access for the copy; 136 GB at ~1-2 GB/s is a few minutes if the source is read while PG is down).
2. Move the other write-heavy trees off root the way .gitnexus was moved (D-020, fstab bind mount): .papercusp/dependency-generations, and consider the scratch/log dirs. On xfs with reflink=1, `cp --reflink` between generations on the same fs becomes near-free. [inferred: check xfs reflink=1 with xfs_info first]
3. Make IO de-prioritisation real: (a) nvme0n1 scheduler mq-deadline (it honours ioprio classes since 5.14; builtin here), persisted by a udev rule; and/or (b) delegate io to user@.service (drop-in Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids, then daemon-reload + user-manager re-exec) so IO*BandwidthMax works (blk-throttle works with any scheduler). Measure w_await / IO PSI before and after; revert is one write.
4. Root at 90% on a DRAM-less drive: free space helps its GC. Consider a daily fstrim (or discard) on /.

Do NOT: stop kopia or the release pipeline by hand; both are legitimate jobs. The fix is placement and priority, not killing them.
_claimSubjectBaseline.title: Root disk is a 90%-full budget DRAM-less NVMe (TEAM TM8FPW002T) with 785 ms write waits; Postgres data+WAL, $HOME and all release copies live on it while the 8 TB SN850X sits fast and 24% free. Every IO de-prioritisation in our user units is also inert.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 on avi-test (pc-host-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72-877db740-vm, r62b 0.0.21-p318r62b), serial console (.papercusp/scratch/avi-test-serial-r62b.txt), su-be77f2f5, P-318:
- 11:16:27Z GCE start. 11:18:04Z startup-script [workspace-host-bootstrap] phase:verify-release, 11:18:51Z phase:install-runtime, 11:19:21Z phase:migrate-database + phase:configure-service.
- papercusp-desktop.socket and papercusp-workspace.service were already active at 11:18:56Z, so desktop.start succeeded: papercusp-desktop@0-694-999 started 11:18:58Z (desktop 0f9dadb3, watch probe reached desktop.ready 11:19:11Z).
- 11:19:23Z the bootstrap restarted papercusp-workspace.service. papercusp-desktop@.service has BindsTo=papercusp-workspace.service, so systemd stopped the desktop first. The customer's desktop was gone 25 s after it opened. The bootstrap completed at 11:19:54Z.
- The same restart also ends any terminal or agent session the customer opened in that window [inferred from the unit stop; not separately measured].

Impact: after any reboot, whatever a customer opens in roughly the first 3 minutes is killed without explanation. 'Units active' is not a readiness signal, which also misled the P-318 r62b avi-test acceptance script.

Fix options: (a) skip the reinstall and restart on a boot where the installed release already matches the manifest (verify-release passes, same storage:current), and only restart when something actually changed; or (b) keep papercusp-workspace from accepting desktop or session starts until the bootstrap writes its completion marker. (a) also removes about 110 s of redundant work on every boot.

Not a P-318 shipment blocker [self-imposed judgement, su-be77f2f5]: the desktop works once the bootstrap completes, and the reboot plus desktop.start acceptance passes.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-01 by su-72d22e0c: a broad read-only `pgrep -af` matched peer launch commands and surfaced full kickoff text plus a possible `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_TOKEN` assignment. Do not copy the observed value. Source measurement: `spawnHeadless` creates `launchEnv` containing `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_PATH` and `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_TOKEN`, then passes that same object to `buildConsoleOneliner`; `buildConsoleOneliner` serializes every env entry as `export KEY='value'` inside the `bash -lc` argument. The same `launchEnv` is already passed through `spawn(...,{env})`, so putting the proof material in argv is redundant. The proof is random per launch, its parent wait is capped at 30 seconds, and `cleanupKickoffProofRequest` unlinks the unique 0600 receipt path after the wait; therefore the specific observed token has no durable revocation surface and is unusable once that path is gone. The systemic defect is the argv exposure during the active launch window (and accidental ingestion into logs/LLM context), which can permit same-UID proof forgery before cleanup. Durable fix: keep the proof path/token out of the oneliner argv while preserving them in the child environment, audit the headless launch-only env boundary for any other values violating `ConsoleEnvelope.env`'s documented non-secret invariant, and add canonical `console-spawn` tests that assert proof path/token are absent from `[bin,...args]`, present only in the child env, and the native kickoff receipt still succeeds. This is the same secret-in-argv defect class previously fixed on other surfaces in WI-41140 and EI-21270327070599812, but this headless console-spawn path remains exposed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-20115751074601731 durable disk-headroom probe: the filesystem containing PostgreSQL data path '/var/lib/postgresql/18/main' is 100% used (warn threshold 90%). A full shared root volume takes PostgreSQL down fleet-wide by preventing WAL, lock, and data-directory writes.

trend: losing 0.63 GiB/h over the last 1.0h — ETA TO FULL ~7h at this rate

ACTION: inspect current filesystem consumers and free space before starting disk-heavy work. This probe is detection-only; it never deletes files or restarts PostgreSQL.

df output:
/dev/nvme0n1p2  1966788624 1941918128   4861160     100% /

LARGEST RELATIONS RIGHT NOW (read at alert time, not written down — see below):
  39.53 GiB  harness_shared.session_archive_files
  18.21 GiB  harness_shared.session_turns
  16.06 GiB  harness_shared.tool_invocations
  11.84 GiB  harness_shared.session_turn_chunks
  9.89 GiB  harness_shared.coord_thread_posts
  6.95 GiB  harness_shared.session_turn_parts

A relation flagged LIKELY TOAST BLOAT is the cheapest win available and needs no owner
decision: its bytes are almost entirely dead TOAST pages that plain VACUUM can never
return to the OS. Confirm by comparing pg_total_relation_size(reltoastrelid) against the
live payload (sum a denormalized length column, or sample pg_column_size), then reclaim
with a rewrite. ALWAYS bound the lock, because a rewrite takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and a
blocked one queues AHEAD of every later lock request on that table:
  sudo -n -u postgres env PGOPTIONS='-c lock_timeout=10000' psql -p 5432 -d papercusp \
    -c 'VACUUM (FULL, VERBOSE, ANALYZE) <schema>.<relation>'
Measured 2026-09-02 (WI-2140986): that reclaimed 60.89 GiB from gateway_payload_blobs in
55s with no contention and no data loss.

INVESTIGATION RECIPE (traps verified while working WI-38595, 2026-08-14, and WI-2141004, 2026-09-02):
1. PostgreSQL is usually NOT the consumer, despite this alarm's title — but "not PostgreSQL" is a HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, never a conclusion to inherit. The probe watches the VOLUME holding PGDATA, and that volume is shared with $HOME. Size PGDATA with 'sudo -n du -xsh /var/lib/postgresql/18/main' — an unprivileged du prints a SILENT '4.0K' (permission denied) rather than an error, which reads as 'Postgres is tiny' for the wrong reason. Start from the LARGEST RELATIONS block above and from a fresh directory scan; do not start from any remembered figure, including one quoted in an older issue. This step used to carry a measured example here, and it went stale and misdirected three work-items for three weeks.
2. CONFIRM WHICH VOLUME a directory is on before reclaiming anything: 'findmnt -T <path>' or 'stat -c %d <path>'. On this box /tmp is a BIND MOUNT from a second physical disk, so deleting 136 GiB of stale /tmp scratch frees exactly nothing on the volume this alarm is about.
3. Enumerate consumers in ONE bounded backgrounded pass: 'nice -n 19 ionice -c3 du -x -d3 / | sort -hr > /tmp/scan-1.txt' (~7 min here). Re-run it later into scan-2.txt and DIFF the two — a diff of two snapshots is the only reliable attribution of NET growth per directory.
4. Do NOT attribute growth by mtime ('find -newermt'). It counts a file's WHOLE size when the file is merely touched, so a single live VM image reads as hundreds of GiB 'written' in 26h. Note also that qcow2 images grow monotonically and never return space the guest frees — and the .img suffix lies, so check the magic ('QFI\373' = qcow2).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Split from WI-6554700010008868 (su-8cec8a78, 2026-10-12).

Measured: with the committed-source loader in NODE_OPTIONS (which `npm run test:file` sets), `npx tsx scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts --input <file> --json` exits 1 in a clean as-committed root (afc18a086c) with `COMMITTED_SOURCE refused scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts: a checkout module was loaded through CommonJS, which bypasses the committed-source check` (scripts/lib/committed-source-loader.mjs:250). Without the loader it exits 0. The root has no package type, so tsx compiles a root `scripts/*.ts` as CJS. The repo convention for scripts that tests spawn is `.mts` (scripts/state-census-roots.mts, state-census-units.mts), which load through ESM and pass the check.

Effect: packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/startup-cache-real-journal.test.ts fails under `npm run test:file` (testing:run and the gate's test:affected do not put the loader in NODE_OPTIONS, so they pass).

Fix: rename to scripts/measure-startup-cache.mts and update package.json `measure:startup-cache`, the test's spawn args, and the reviewed bypass entry in scripts/check-resource-governor-enforcement.mjs (~line 1872). Recurrence guard: a test that fails when any *.test.ts spawns tsx on a root `scripts/<name>.ts` (CJS) path.

DEFERRED until plan token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 ships [self-imposed]: the rename changes the blobs of P-001's audited evidence files (test + script cited in code-truth audit #4 and bound to SPEC-P-001 / AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001), which would force re-binding and re-audit right before acceptance grading.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[measured 2026-10-14T02:33Z, harness_shared.tool_invocations, workspace papercusp-workspace, last 5h] locks:release: 482 ok, 44 invalid-input from 16 owners, first 2026-10-13T21:34:34Z, latest 02:32:15Z. All 44 have one cause, `Unrecognized key: "retain"`, and all were served by port-3070, build d740fc3802.

[measured] Source: posttooluse-locks-release.sh:592 and posttoolbatch-locks-release.sh:484 send {retain:true, native_edit_proof} to attribute a native edit made under an explicitly held lock. The packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/release.ts blob carrying `retain` is on staging (6958ed5d1f, commit 7c7c4a2923, 2026-10-13T01:44Z). main and the deployed d740fc3802 both carry cea7db3c42, which has no retain support (grep marker retain_requires_native_edit_proof: staging 1, main 0, d740fc3802 0).

[measured, from source] The impact is bounded and by design: release.ts:88-94 sends no `paths`, so an operator that predates `retain` refuses the request and releases no lock. The explicit hold survives. What is lost is the native-edit attribution in the ledger, and each refusal adds an invalid-input row to tool error rates.

Close condition: after :3070 serves a build whose release.ts contains retain_requires_native_edit_proof (state:read deploy.3070.sha, then dev:pipeline_position { path:'packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/release.ts' } -> positions.deployed:true), re-run the same tool_invocations query. The `Unrecognized key: "retain"` count after the deploy time should be 0, and ok release rows with attributed paths should appear. If refusals continue after deploy, reclassify this as a bug.

Residue of WI-6554700010011168 (comment 1179642 listed release-argument errors as residue).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[owner:Avi 2026-10-21 directive #2149] asked: can we use our code-intelligence tools to also enhance our relevancy router?

Measured today (su-611f037a): packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router.ts blends similarity 0.55 / verification 0.15 / authorship 0.15. Authorship (lines ~1283-1299) only fires when extractPathTokens finds a literal path in the question, and then matches it by ILIKE substring against payload->'paths' of the candidate's COMMITTED work-items. Over the last 30 days 263 of 3966 persisted routings (6.6%, consult_state, all workspaces) had any candidate with authorship > 0.

Proposal:
1. Resolve the question to code subjects, not just literal paths: identifiers -> defining files via lsp:query workspace_symbols / the graph index, plus explicit paths; optional 1-hop graph neighbourhood (callers/impact) at reduced weight.
2. Source authorship from what agents actually did: edit_attribution_ledger edits per owner per file (strong) and code reads/lsp/graph queries from tool_invocations (weak 'familiarity'), the same inputs deriveCodeWorkingSet uses. Count all-time (D-007), no recency term (D-001 structural rule), and keep simFloor so track record cannot promote an irrelevant agent (D-003).
3. Reuse in acceptance-grader selection: edit attribution also identifies implementers who must be excluded.
4. Evaluate offline first: replay persisted consult_state.routing snapshots with the new signal and compare rankings and no_qualified_responder rates before changing weights.

Needs a plan (several items: subject resolution, signal source, grader-exclusion reuse, offline eval, weight calibration).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Owned residue of WI-6554700010029298. That item fixed ONE root cause: DRAIN was a caller-only overlay lost at leader succession, and governor top-ups launched members without any mode. The fix persists the fleet launch mode on agent_fleets.headcount_config.mode. These member-discipline findings from the same scorecard are NOT explained by missing DRAIN and still need their own investigation. Source: fleet-execution-health rev45 scorecard of fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-0930, window 2026-10-19T07Z..10-26T07Z (EI-27027117442590045 / WI-6554700010029288). Evidence SQL: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/feh/ev3-ev6.sql.

Findings:
1. Comms volume: 18,083 member coord messages / 638 closes = 28.3 per close; 21.8% duplicate content.
2. Observation volume: 4,712 observation-lane filings = 7.4 per close (+518 work filings, 0.81/close). Question: should turn-end observation capture be rate-limited per close for fleet members?
3. Responsiveness: 22.1% of 371 directed leader asks got no reply within 2h.
4. Claim discipline: 8 force-claims; 1 complete-after-claim_conflict; 1 of 3 stand-down orders followed by a new claim.
5. Ledger hygiene: 59/638 closes with first_claimed_at NULL; 47/638 closes at authority=proposed.
6. Context: 132 of 670 active members took >=2 Compaction over-limit notices.

First step: re-measure after the DRAIN fix reaches :3070 and the Luna Max members relaunch under mode=drain. DRAIN suppresses incidental filing, so finding 2 may shrink by itself; the rest need their own root cause. [inferred] that DRAIN affects only finding 2.

(1) member-productivity: 28 closes / 440.3 active seat-hours = 0.064 per hour (7-day baseline 0.18); 40 of 57 members with >=2 active seat-hours closed nothing. The admitted frontier is not empty (~1,410 admitted unheld bug/change, raw SQL), so starvation does not explain it. Members hold 131 non-terminal items (1,149 claimed-but-unclosed item-hours), 55 blocked (45 runtime live-dependency). (2) member-liveness: fleet:status 20:01Z shows 9 parked members, and loop:status on each reports active:false, rewakeGuaranteed:false (idle 15 min to 4.8h: su-d944f431, su-55e68e71, su-47ae7149, su-7f8aed23, su-6a3d50d5, a su-respawn-* member, 3 more). Leader made 0 coord:wake/dispatch calls in the window. (3) membership-churn: 9 member joins in 9.4h (~23/day vs target 50). Unknown cause: where member seat-time goes (repeat blocker reports are 64% of member messages per WI-6554700010029331) and why parked members lose their loop. Next: classify seat-time of the 40 zero-close members by tool family, and check why parked members' loops are inactive (loop ended vs never armed after respawn). _claimSubjectBaseline.body: [self-imposed under owner #2494, su-96b7fe62] lint:reachable-advisories went red on frozen candidate 8c03b5dcd156 because the advisory database moved, not because code changed. Measured 2026-10-27 13:05Z with scripts/check-reachable-advisories.mjs --strict: tip (shared tree) has 10 NEW offenders, the frozen lineage (precheck worktree at 57b527a653) has 11 (tip's 10 plus follow-redirects, which tip's newer lockfile already fixes). Patch-eligible: next (CRITICAL), undici, body-parser, follow-redirects. Semver-major: @azure/identity + @azure/msal-node (fix @azure/identity@4.13.0), astro-robots-txt (0.2.0), dompurify CRITICAL (via monaco-editor@0.57.0), mem0ai + openai + zod (via mem0ai@1.0.39). All 11 were added to scripts/reachable-advisories-baseline.json only to keep a lockfile change off the frozen-candidate repair, following the js-yaml / @bundled-es-modules/glob precedent (WI-10006989). WORK: on staging, run npm run install:safe -- update for the patch-eligible packages, upgrade the semver-major ones where the owners allow, re-run the checker, and remove each entry once it reports STALE. Also prune the 8 entries already STALE at tip (@bundled-es-modules/glob, @excalidraw/excalidraw, chokidar, fast-glob, find-yarn-workspace-root, micromatch, patch-package, sass) once main has advanced past the frozen lineage.

A newer receipt now supersedes it for current behavior: audit row 9a9688c7-e5aa-4f18-9ca5-fe191df63f7a, run dd4db4b3-6937-4f79-931f-01e8a05dcb3a, 2026-10-28 08:12:48.371Z–08:27:48.487Z, dryRun=false, complete=false. Aggregate reacquireMutexWaitMs=515076ms; its recorded mutexTimeout is phase=reacquire, waitedMs=3918 vs timeout/remaining budget 3814ms. That timeout's measured subphases are ticket-scan=621.4ms, backoff-sleep=3294.4ms, abandoned-lock.owner-read=64.2ms, process-probe=0.08ms, process-identity=1.68ms. Therefore the newer timeout is dominated by ticket scanning and backoff, not owner-file reads; do not generalize this to the older receipt. The same receipt has multiple stale/changed census errors and failed delegates, so the mutex timeout is not established as the sole cause of complete=false. Root cause remains unknown. Read the fs-mutex queue-wait writer and obtain fresh admitted evidence before changing code; do not attribute to general resource pressure. The current health probe showed the bg-host ticker advancing and the default mutex directory absent, so no restart was indicated. Related completed WI-6554700010023014 fixed missing-holder diagnostics; EI-26942454413534533 fixed a FIFO-yield behavior, but neither proves the cause of this newer timing profile.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[owner:Avi 2026-10-28 #2574] "Is there any justification to have these timeouts? Is there any reason not to remove all timeouts and just let all the main greening things go to completion with no time limit anywhere?" (also #2569: 'i thought we removed all timeouts?').

MEASURED (su-96b7fe62, 2026-10-28 ~15:05Z, source read): the run-level wall clock is GREEN_CHECKPOINT_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS = 115m (packages/operator-core/lib/release/green-checkpoint-schedule.ts:129). Its only stated rationale is the hourly cron slot (a run past HH+2:15 makes that fire skip). Derived from it: MANUAL_CHECKPOINT_WATCHDOG_MS + CHECKPOINT_MAX_RUNTIME_SEC RuntimeMaxSec backstop + REPLACE_STALE_MIN_AGE_SEC (release-checkpoint-launch.ts), DEFAULT_REFIRE_RUN_BUDGET_MS 110m, resolveQualificationYieldBudget quantum + TASK_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS export (green-checkpoint.ts:4550-4554, 11319), the affected-tests deadline-insufficient refusal (scripts/affected-tests.mjs via scripts/lib/task-deadline.mjs + budgeted-task-scheduler.mjs), DEPENDENCY_GENERATION_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS 90m. release-timing-invariants.test.ts pins the chain.

PLAN: (1) remove the run-level wall clock and everything derived from it on the gate path (no RuntimeMaxSec, no deadline export, no deadline-insufficient refusal for gate runs); (2) replace wall-clock wedge/replaceStale with a NO-PROGRESS detector (no test completions + no output + no cgroup CPU for N min); (3) KEEP per-test timeouts (VITEST_UNIT_TIMEOUT_MS etc.) and idle-timeouts, which fail one unit and keep the run going; (4) update release-timing-invariants.test.ts to pin the new invariant (no run-level wall clock on the gate path) instead of the ordering of the old numbers.

WHY NOW: with reuse at 0 (WI-6554700010030941) the full-suite estimate exceeds the 115m budget, so the runner refuses and the gate measures nothing.

rows.title: Managed continuation loses guaranteed loop re-wake after a delivered fire without a loop-origin turn

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary: Fixed direct loop-fire turn correlation to require the exact envelope nonce together with routine id and wake count. Added real-Postgres regression coverage for wrong-nonce rejection and a true prompt whose turn-start marker is timestamped later.
terminalCompletionEvidence.testResult: Run 23607243 passed 4/4; the wrong-nonce case stayed unlinked and exact nonce matched despite marker timestamp order.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: The direct loop-fire join correlated a prompt to a turn-start marker by timestamp ordering. The prompt row can be timestamped before its marker even when both belong to the same loop turn; a later prompt with a wrong nonce can also satisfy timestamp ordering.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: Before the fix, run 23604777 failed the wrong-nonce assertion: expected null, received 2026-11-08T06:12:27.273Z. After the fix, run 23607243 passed all 4 cases.
rootCauseVerification.testProcedure: npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-turn-start-reconcile.integration.test.ts; the file uses a disposable real-Postgres fixture and exercises getLoopStatus against persisted prompt and marker rows.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: Run 23604777 linked the wrong-nonce row. In run 23607243, the wrong nonce stayed unlinked and the exact nonce was recognized with the marker timestamp after the prompt.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Use the real-Postgres fixture to record one exact loop-fire marker, insert a wrong-nonce prompt at a later timestamp and assert lastLoopTurnAt is null, then insert the exact-nonce prompt at a timestamp earlier than its marker and assert the loop turn is recognized.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The real loop-fire prompt had no valid turn-start marker, so lastLoopTurnAt was correctly null; the timestamp difference was incidental.

predictedObservations.hypothesis: Timestamp-only matching links the later wrong-nonce prompt and misses the exact-nonce prompt when its marker timestamp follows the prompt. Exact nonce plus routine id and wake count rejects the wrong prompt and links the exact prompt despite timestamp order.
predictedObservations.alternativeHypothesis: Without a valid marker for the prompt, neither prompt links regardless of timestamp; changing timestamp order does not change the result.

No `resources` glob in any of the six tauri config variants covers that path — every glob is rooted at src-tauri/SIDECAR/, a different directory. What ships is generated: bin/stage-env-sidecars.sh does `rm -rf $SIDECAR/env-sidecars` then `cp -al $SIDECAR/spa $ENV_SC/spa`, hardlink-copying the PRIMARY sidecar SPA, which does not contain these pages. bin/build-windows-cross.sh independently rm -rf's and re-stages the top-level dir before building.

Root cause of the residue: that directory is a committed BUILD ARTIFACT the build regenerates. Independently corroborated by EI-20555742146560765, which measured 4,483 tracked files under the same path and 2,418 self-dirtied entries during the 0.0.17 release cut. The two pages were stale content dating to 2026-07-07, from when the primary SPA still had them.

My own instrument error, recorded so it does not recur: the initial `git ls-files | grep el-` was run from the SUPERPROJECT and returned nothing, which made tracked files look like untracked stray output. git ls-files does not recurse into submodules and papercusp-desktop is one.
